verses.text: \sc In\sc* the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth as ithout form, and void; and darkness \add as\add* upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the aters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there as light.
And God sa the light, that \add it as\add* good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning ere the first day.
And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the aters, and let it divide the aters from the aters.
And God made the firmament, and divided the aters hich \add ere\add* under the firmament from the aters hich \add ere\add* above the firmament: and it as so.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning ere the second day.
And God said, Let the aters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry \add land\add* appear: and it as so.
And God called the dry \add land\add* Earth; and the gathering together of the aters called he Seas: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, \add and\add* the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, hose seed \add is\add* in itself, upon the earth: and it as so.

And the earth brought forth grass, \add and\add* herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, hose seed \add as\add* in itself, after his kind: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.
And the evening and the morning ere the third day.
And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
and let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it as so.
And God made to great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: \add he made\add* the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,
and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.
And the evening and the morning ere the fourth day.
And God said, Let the aters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fol \add that\add* may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.

And God created great hales, and every living creature that moveth, hich the aters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every inged fol after his kind: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.
And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the aters in the seas, and let fol multiply in the earth.
And the evening and the morning ere the fifth day.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it as so.
And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God sa that \add it as\add* good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fol of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
So God created man in his on image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fol of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, hich \add is\add* upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the hich \add is\add* the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.

And to every beast of the earth, and to every fol of the air, and to every \add thing\add* that creepeth upon the earth, herein \add there is\add* life, \add I have given\add* every green herb for meat: and it as so.
And God sa every thing that he had made, and behold, \add it as\add* very good. And the evening and the morning ere the sixth day.
Thus the heavens and the earth ere finished, and all the host of them.
And on the seventh day God ended his ork hich he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his ork hich he had made.
And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his ork hich God created and made.
These \add are\add* the generations of the heavens and of the earth hen they ere created, in the day that the \sc Lord\sc* God made the earth and the heavens,

and every plant of the field before it as in the earth, and every herb of the field before it gre: for the \sc Lord\sc* God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and \add there as\add* not a man to till the ground.
But there ent up a mist from the earth, and atered the hole face of the ground.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God formed man \add of\add* the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God planted a garden eastard in Eden; and there he put the man hom he had formed.

And out of the ground made the \sc Lord\sc* God to gro every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knoledge of good and evil.
And a river ent out of Eden to ater the garden; and from thence it as parted, and became into four heads.
The name of the first \add is\add* Pison: that \add is it\add* hich compasseth the hole land of Havilah, here \add there is\add* gold;
and the gold of that land \add is\add* good: there \add is\add* bdellium and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river \add is\add* Gihon: the same \add is it\add* that compasseth the hole land of Ethiopia.
And the name of the third river \add is\add* Hiddekel: that \add is it\add* hich goeth toard the east of Assyria. And the fourth river \add is\add* Euphrates.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
but of the tree of the knoledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God said, \add It is\add* not good that the man should be alone; I ill make him a help meet for him.

And out of the ground the \sc Lord\sc* God formed every beast of the field, and every fol of the air; and brought \add them\add* unto Adam to see hat he ould call them: and hatsoever Adam called every living creature, that \add as\add* the name thereof.
And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fol of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there as not found a help meet for him.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;
and the rib, hich the \sc Lord\sc* God had taken from man, made he a oman, and brought her unto the man.
And Adam said, This \add is\add* no bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she as taken out of Man.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his ife: and they shall be one flesh.
And they ere both naked, the man and his ife, and ere not ashamed.
No the serpent as more subtil than any beast of the field hich the \sc Lord\sc* God had made. And he said unto the oman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the oman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
but of the fruit of the tree hich \add is\add* in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the oman, Ye shall not surely die:
for God doth kno that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knoing good and evil.

And hen the oman sa that the tree \add as\add* good for food, and that it \add as\add* pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make \add one\add* ise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband ith her; and he did eat.
And the eyes of them both ere opened, and they kne that they \add ere\add* naked; and they seed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

And they heard the voice of the \sc Lord\sc* God alking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his ife hid themselves from the presence of the \sc Lord\sc* God amongst the trees of the garden.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where \add art\add* thou?
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I as afraid, because I \add as\add* naked; and I hid myself.
And he said, Who told thee that thou \add ast\add* naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, hereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
And the man said, The oman hom thou gavest \add to be\add* ith me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God said unto the oman, What \add is\add* this \add that\add* thou hast done? And the oman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

And the \sc Lord\sc* God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou \add art\add* cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
and I ill put enmity beteen thee and the oman, and beteen thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
Unto the oman he said, I ill greatly multiply thy sorro and thy conception; in sorro thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire \add shall be\add* to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy ife, and hast eaten of the tree, of hich I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed \add is\add* the ground for thy sake; in sorro shalt thou eat \add of\add* it all the days of thy life;
thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
in the seat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it ast thou taken: for dust thou \add art\add*, and unto dust shalt thou return.
And Adam called his ife’s name Eve; because she as the mother of all living.
Unto Adam also and to his ife did the \sc Lord\sc* God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
And the \sc Lord\sc* God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to kno good and evil: and no, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
therefore the \sc Lord\sc* God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from hence he as taken.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sord hich turned every ay, to keep the ay of the tree of life.
And Adam kne Eve his ife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the \sc Lord\sc*.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel as a keeper of sheep, but Cain as a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the \sc Lord\sc* had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain as very roth, and his countenance fell.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said unto Cain, Why art thou roth? and hy is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest ell, \add shalt thou\add* not be accepted? and if thou doest not ell, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee \add shall be\add* his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
And Cain talked ith Abel his brother: and it came to pass, hen they ere in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and sle him.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said unto Cain, Where \add is\add* Abel thy brother? And he said, I kno not: \add Am\add* I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
And no \add art\add* thou cursed from the earth, hich hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand.
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
And Cain said unto the \sc Lord\sc*, My punishment \add is\add* greater than \add I\add* can bear.

Behold, thou hast driven me out \add this\add* day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, \add that\add* every one that findeth me shall slay me.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said unto him, Therefore hosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the \sc Lord\sc* set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
And Cain ent out from the presence of the \sc Lord\sc*, and delt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain kne his ife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
And unto Enoch as born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.
And Lamech took unto him to ives: the name of the one \add as\add* Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Adah bare Jabal: he as the father of such as dell in tents, and \add of such as have\add* cattle.
And his brother’s name \add as\add* Jubal: he as the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain \add as\add* Naamah.
And Lamech said unto his ives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; Ye ives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: For I have slain a man to my ounding, And a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, Truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And Adam kne his ife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, \add said she\add*, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, hom Cain sle.
And to Seth, \add to\add* him also there as born a son; and he called his name Enos; then began \add men\add* to call upon the name of the \sc Lord\sc*.
This \add is\add* the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day hen they ere created.
And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat \add a son\add* in his on likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
and the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth ere eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters:
and all the days that Adam lived ere nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
And Seth lived an hundred and five years, and begat Enos:
and Seth lived after he begat Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Seth ere nine hundred and telve years: and he died.
And Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan:
and Enos lived after he begat Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Enos ere nine hundred and five years: and he died.
And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel:
and Cainan lived after he begat Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Cainan ere nine hundred and ten years: and he died.
And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:
and Mahalaleel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Mahalaleel ere eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died.
And Jared lived an hundred sixty and to years, and he begat Enoch:
and Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Jared ere nine hundred sixty and to years: and he died.
And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
and Enoch alked ith God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Enoch ere three hundred sixty and five years:
and Enoch alked ith God: and he \add as\add* not; for God took him.
And Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech:
and Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and to years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Methuselah ere nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.
And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and to years, and begat a son:
and he called his name Noah, saying, This \add same\add* shall comfort us concerning our ork and toil of our hands, because of the ground hich the \sc Lord\sc* hath cursed.
And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Lamech ere seven hundred seventy and seven years: and he died.
And Noah as five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it came to pass, hen men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters ere born unto them,
that the sons of God sa the daughters of men that they \add ere\add* fair; and they took them ives of all hich they chose.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said, My spirit shall not alays strive ith man, for that he also \add is\add* flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and tenty years.

There ere giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, hen the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare \add children\add* to them, the same \add became\add* mighty \add men\add* hich \add ere\add* of old, men of renon.
And \sc God\sc* sa that the ickedness of man \add as\add* great in the earth, and \add that\add* every imagination of the thoughts of his heart \add as\add* only evil continually.
And it repented the \sc Lord\sc* that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.

And the \sc Lord\sc* said, I ill destroy man hom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fols of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the \sc Lord\sc*.
These \add are\add* the generations of Noah: Noah as a just man \add and\add* perfect in his generations, \add and\add* Noah alked ith God.
And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth also as corrupt before God, and the earth as filled \add ith\add* violence.
And God looked upon the earth, and behold, it as corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his ay upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled \add ith\add* violence through them; and behold, I ill destroy them ith the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher ood; rooms shalt thou make \add in\add* the ark, and shalt pitch it ithin and ithout ith pitch.

And this \add is the fashion\add* hich thou shalt make it \add of:\add* the length of the ark \add shall be\add* three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.

A indo shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; \add ith\add* loer, second, and third \add stories\add* shalt thou make it.

And behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of aters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, herein \add is\add* the breath of life, from under heaven; \add and\add* every \add thing\add* that \add is\add* in the earth shall die.
But ith thee ill I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy ife, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.
And of every living \add thing\add* of all flesh, to of every \add sort\add* shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep \add them\add* alive ith thee; they shall be male and female.
Of fols after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the earth after his kind, to of every \add sort\add* shall come unto thee, to keep \add them\add* alive.
And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather \add it\add* to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the male and his female: and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean by to, the male and his female.
Of fols also of the air by sevens, the male and the female; to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth.
For yet seven days, \add and\add* I ill cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living substance that I have made ill I destroy from off the face of the earth.
And Noah did according unto all that the \sc Lord\sc* commanded him.
And Noah \add as\add* six hundred years old hen the flood of aters as upon the earth.
And Noah ent in, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him, into the ark, because of the aters of the flood.
Of clean beasts, and of beasts that \add are\add* not clean, and of fols, and of every \add thing\add* that creepeth upon the earth,
there ent in to and to unto Noah into the ark, the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah.
And it came to pass after seven days, that the aters of the flood ere upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day ere all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the indos of heaven ere opened.
And the rain as upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s ife, and the three ives of his sons ith them, into the ark;

they, and every beast after his kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind, and every fol after his kind, every bird of every sort.
And they ent in unto Noah into the ark, to and to of all flesh, herein \add is\add* the breath of life.
And they that ent in, ent in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the \sc Lord\sc* shut him in.
And the flood as forty days upon the earth; and the aters increased, and bare up the ark, and it as lift up above the earth.
And the aters prevailed, and ere increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark ent upon the face of the aters.
And the aters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that \add ere\add* under the hole heaven, ere covered.
Fifteen cubits upard did the aters prevail; and the mountains ere covered.
And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, \add both\add* of fol, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
all in hose nostrils \add as\add* the breath of life, of all that \add as\add* in the dry \add land\add*, died.

And every living substance as destroyed hich \add as\add* upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fol of the heaven; and they ere destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained \add alive\add*, and \add they\add* that \add ere\add* ith him in the ark.
And the aters prevailed upon the earth an hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that \add as\add* ith him in the ark: and God made a ind to pass over the earth, and the aters assaged;
the fountains also of the deep and the indos of heaven ere stopped, and the rain from heaven as restrained;
and the aters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of the hundred and fifty days the aters ere abated.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the aters decreased continually until the tenth month: in the tenth \add month\add*, on the first \add day\add* of the month, ere the tops of the mountains seen.
And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the indo of the ark hich he had made:
and he sent forth a raven, hich ent forth to and fro, until the aters ere dried up from off the earth.
Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the aters ere abated from off the face of the ground;

but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark, for the aters \add ere\add* on the face of the hole earth: then he put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in unto him into the ark.
And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;
and the dove came in to him in the evening; and lo, in her mouth \add as\add* an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah kne that the aters ere abated from off the earth.
And he stayed yet other seven days; and sent forth the dove; hich returned not again unto him any more.

And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first \add month\add*, the first \add day\add* of the month, the aters ere dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground as dry.
And in the second month, on the seven and tentieth day of the month, as the earth dried.
And God spake unto Noah, saying,
Go forth of the ark, thou, and thy ife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.

Bring forth ith thee every living thing that \add is\add* ith thee, of all flesh, \add both\add* of fol, and of cattle, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.
And Noah ent forth, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him:
every beast, every creeping thing, and every fol, \add and\add* hatsoever creepeth upon the earth, after their kinds, ent forth out of the ark.
And Noah builded an altar unto the \sc Lord\sc*; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fol, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

And the \sc Lord\sc* smelled a seet savour; and the \sc Lord\sc* said in his heart, I ill not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart \add is\add* evil from his youth; neither ill I again smite any more every \add thing\add* living, as I have done.
While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and inter, and day and night shall not cease.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fol of the air, upon all that moveth \add upon\add* the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.
Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; \add even\add* as the green herb have I given you all \add things\add*.
But flesh ith the life thereof, \add hich is\add* the blood thereof, shall you not eat.
And surely your blood of your lives ill I require; at the hand of every beast ill I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother ill I require the life of man.
Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons ith him, saying,
And I, behold I establish my covenant ith you and ith your seed after you;
and ith every living creature that \add is\add* ith you, of the fol, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth ith you; from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
And I ill establish my covenant ith you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the aters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said, This \add is\add* the token of the covenant hich I make beteen me and you and every living creature that \add is\add* ith you, for perpetual generations:
I do set my bo in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant beteen me and the earth.

And the men rose up from thence, and looked toard Sodom: and Abraham ent ith them to bring them on the ay.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said, Shall I hide from Abraham \add that thing\add* hich I do;
seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I kno him, that he ill command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the ay of the \sc Lord\sc*, to do justice and judgment; that the \sc Lord\sc* may bring upon Abraham that hich he hath spoken of him.
And the \sc Lord\sc* said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;
I ill go don no, and see hether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, hich is come unto me; and if not, I ill kno.
And the men turned their faces from thence, and ent toard Sodom: but Abraham stood yet before the \sc Lord\sc*.
And Abraham dre near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous ith the icked?
Peradventure there be fifty righteous ithin the city: ilt thou also destroy and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that \add are\add* therein?

That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous ith the icked: and that the righteous should be as the icked, that be far from thee: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
And the \sc Lord\sc* said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous ithin the city, then I ill spare all the place for their sakes.
And Abraham ansered and said, Behold no, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, hich \add am but\add* dust and ashes:
Peradventure there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: ilt thou destroy all the city for \add lack of\add* five? And he said, If I find there forty and five, I ill not destroy \add it\add*.
And he spake unto him yet again, and said, Peradventure there shall be forty found there. And he said, I ill not do \add it\add* for forty’s sake.
And he said \add unto him\add*, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I ill speak: Peradventure there shall thirty be found there. And he said, I ill not do \add it\add*, if I find thirty there.
And he said, Behold no, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: Peradventure there shall be tenty found there. And he said, I ill not destroy \add it\add* for tenty’s sake.
And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I ill speak yet but \add this\add* once: Peradventure ten shall be found there. And he said, I ill not destroy \add it\add* for ten’s sake.
And the \sc Lord\sc* ent his ay, as soon as he had left communing ith Abraham: and Abraham returned unto his place.
And there came to angels to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot seeing \add them\add* rose up to meet them; and he boed himself ith his face toard the ground;

and he said, Behold no, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and ash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ays. And they said, Nay; but e ill abide in the street all night.
And he pressed upon them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.
But before they lay don, the men of the city, \add even\add* the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
and they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where \add are\add* the men hich came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that e may kno them.
And Lot ent out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him,
and said, I pray you, brethren, do not \add so\add* ickedly.

Behold no, I have to daughters hich have not knon man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do ye to them as \add is\add* good in your eyes: only unto these men do nothing; for therefore came they under the shado of my roof.

And they said, Stand back. And they said \add again\add*, \add This\add* one \add fello\add* came in to sojourn, and he ill needs be a judge: no ill e deal orse ith thee, than ith them. And they pressed sore upon the man, \add even\add* Lot, and came near to break the door.
But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.
And they smote the men that \add ere at\add* the door of the house ith blindness, both small and great; so that they earied themselves to find the door.
And the men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son in la, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and hatsoever thou hast in the city, bring \add them\add* out of this place:
for e ill destroy \add this\add* place, because the cry of them is axen great before the face of the \sc Lord\sc*; and the \sc Lord\sc* hath sent us to destroy it.

And Lot ent out, and spake unto his sons in la, hich married his daughters, and said, Up, get ye out of this place; for the \sc Lord\sc* ill destroy this city. But he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in la.
And hen the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy ife, and thy to daughters, hich are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.

And hile he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his ife, and upon the hand of his to daughters; the \sc Lord\sc* being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him ithout the city.

And it came to pass, hen they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.
And Lot said unto them, Oh, not so, my Lord:

behold no, thy servant hath found grace in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy mercy, hich thou hast sheed unto me in saving my life; and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest \add some\add* evil take me, and I die:
behold no, this city \add is\add* near to flee unto, and it \add is\add* a little one: Oh, let me escape thither, (\add is\add* it not a little one?) and my soul shall live.
And he said unto him, See, I have accepted thee concerning this thing, that I ill not overthro \add this\add* city, for the hich thou hast spoken.
Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the city as called Zoar.
The sun as risen upon the earth hen Lot entered into Zoar.
Then the \sc Lord\sc* rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the \sc Lord\sc* out of heaven;
and he overthre those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that hich gre upon the ground.
But his ife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place here he stood before the \sc Lord\sc*:
and he looked toard Sodom and Gomorrah, and toard all the land of the plain, and beheld, and lo, the smoke of the country ent up as the smoke of a furnace.
And it came to pass, hen God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthro, hen he overthre the cities in the hich Lot delt.
And Lot ent up out of Zoar, and delt in the mountain, and his to daughters ith him; for he feared to dell in Zoar: and he delt in a cave, he and his to daughters.
And the firstborn said unto the younger, Our father \add is\add* old, and \add there is\add* not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of all the earth:
come, let us make our father drink ine, and e ill lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night: and the firstborn ent in, and lay ith her father; and he perceived not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.

And it came to pass on the morro, that the firstborn said unto the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight ith my father: let us make him drink ine this night also; and go thou in, \add and\add* lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night also: and the younger arose, and lay ith him; and he perceived not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.
Thus ere both the daughters of Lot ith child by their father.
And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same \add is\add* the father of the Moabites unto \add this\add* day.
And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same \add is\add* the father of the children of Ammon unto \add this\add* day.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toard the south country, and delled beteen Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his ife, She \add is\add* my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou \add art but\add* a dead man, for the oman hich thou hast taken; for she \add is\add* a man’s ife.
But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, ilt thou slay also a righteous nation?
Said he not unto me, She \add is\add* my sister? and she, even she herself said, He \add is\add* my brother: in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands have I done this.
And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I kno that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also ithheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

No therefore restore the man \add his\add* ife; for he \add is\add* a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore \add her\add* not, kno thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that \add are\add* thine.
Therefore Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears: and the men ere sore afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said unto him, What hast thou done unto us? and hat have I offended thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds unto me that ought not to be done.
And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What saest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
And Abraham said, Because I thought, Surely the fear of God \add is\add* not in this place; and they ill slay me for my ife’s sake.
And yet indeed \add she is\add* my sister; she \add is\add* the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my ife.

And it came to pass, hen God caused me to ander from my father’s house, that I said unto her, This \add is\add* thy kindness hich thou shalt she unto me; at every place hither e shall come, say of me, He \add is\add* my brother.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and omenservants, and gave \add them\add* unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his ife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land \add is\add* before thee: dell here it pleaseth thee.

And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand \add pieces\add* of silver: behold, he \add is\add* to thee a covering of the eyes, unto all that \add are\add* ith thee, and ith all \add other:\add* thus she as reproved.
So Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his ife, and his maidservants; and they bare \add children\add*.
For the \sc Lord\sc* had fast closed up all the ombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s ife.
And the \sc Lord\sc* visited Sarah as he had said, and the \sc Lord\sc* did unto Sarah as he had spoken.
For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of hich God had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son that as born unto him, hom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.
And Abraham \add as\add* an hundred years old, hen his son Isaac as born unto him.
And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, \add so that\add* all that hear ill laugh ith me.

And the child gre, and as eaned: and Abraham made a great feast the \add same\add* day that Isaac as eaned.
And Sarah sa the son of Hagar the Egyptian, hich she had born unto Abraham, mocking.
Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bondoman and her son: for the son of this bondoman shall not be heir ith my son, \add even\add* ith Isaac.
And the thing as very grievous in Abraham’s sight because of his son.

And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy bondoman; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of ater, and gave \add it\add* unto Hagar, putting \add it\add* on her shoulder, and the child, and sent her aay: and she departed, and andered in the ilderness of Beer-sheba.

And she ent, and sat her don over against \add him\add* a good ay off, as it ere a boshot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against \add him\add*, and lift up her voice, and ept.

And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad here he \add is\add*.
Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thine hand; for I ill make him a great nation.
And God opened her eyes, and she sa a ell of ater; and she ent, and filled the bottle \add ith\add* ater, and gave the lad drink.

And he delt in the ilderness of Paran: and his mother took him a ife out of the land of Egypt.
And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech and Phichol the chief captain of his host spake unto Abraham, saying, God \add is\add* ith thee in all that thou doest:

no therefore sear unto me here by God that thou ilt not deal falsely ith me, nor ith my son, nor ith my son’s son: \add but\add* according to the kindness that I have done unto thee, thou shalt do unto me, and to the land herein thou hast sojourned.
And Abraham said, I ill sear.
And Abraham reproved Abimelech because of a ell of ater, hich Abimelech’s servants had violently taken aay.
And Abimelech said, I ot not ho hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet heard I \add of it\add*, but to day.

And he said, For \add these\add* seven ee lambs shalt thou take of my hand, that they may be a itness unto me, that I have digged this ell.

And \add Abraham\add* planted a grove in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the \sc Lord\sc*, the everlasting God.

And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, \add here\add* I \add am\add*.

And he said, Take no thy son, thine only \add son\add* Isaac, hom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains hich I ill tell thee of.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took to of his young men ith him, and Isaac his son, and clave the ood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and ent unto the place of hich God had told him.
Then on the third day Abraham lift up his eyes, and sa the place afar off.
And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide you here ith the ass; and I and the lad ill go yonder and orship, and come again to you.

And Abraham said, My son, God ill provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they ent both of them together.
And they came to the place hich God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the ood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the ood.
And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
And the angel of the \sc Lord\sc* called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here \add am\add* I.
And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for no I kno that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not ithheld thy son, thine only \add son\add* from me.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind \add him\add* a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham ent and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said \add to this\add* day, In the mount of the \sc Lord\sc* it shall be seen.
And the angel of the \sc Lord\sc* called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time,
and said, By myself have I sorn, saith the \sc Lord\sc*, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not ithheld thy son, thine only \add son:\add*

that in blessing I ill bless thee, and in multiplying I ill multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand hich \add is\add* upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and ent together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham delt at Beer-sheba.
And it came to pass after these things, that it as told Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she hath also born children unto thy brother Nahor;
Huz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight Milcah did bear to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
And his concubine, hose name \add as\add* Reumah, she bare also Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.
And Sarah as an hundred and seven and tenty years old: \add these ere\add* the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died in Kirjath-arba; the same \add is\add* Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to eep for her.
And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying,
I \add am\add* a stranger and a sojourner ith you: give me a possession of a buryingplace ith you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
And the children of Heth ansered Abraham, saying unto him,
Hear us, my lord: thou \add art\add* a mighty prince among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall ithhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.
And Abraham stood up, and boed himself to the people of the land, \add even\add* to the children of Heth.
And he communed ith them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight; hear me, and intreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, hich he hath, hich \add is\add* in the end of his field; for as much money as it is orth he shall give it me for a possession of a buryingplace amongst you.

And Ephron delt amongst the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite ansered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, \add even\add* of all that ent in \add at\add* the gate of his city, saying,
Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that \add is\add* therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.

And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou \add ilt give it\add*, I pray thee, hear me: I ill give \add thee\add* money for the field; take \add it\add* of me, and I ill bury my dead there.
And Ephron ansered Abraham, saying unto him,
My lord, hearken unto me: the land \add is orth\add* four hundred shekels of silver; hat \add is\add* that betixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.

And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham eighed to Ephron the silver, hich he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current \add money\add* ith the merchant.

And the field of Ephron, hich \add as\add* in Machpelah, hich \add as\add* before Mamre, the field, and the cave hich \add as\add* therein, and all the trees that \add ere\add* in the field, that \add ere\add* in all the borders round about, ere made sure
unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that ent in \add at\add* the gate of his city.
And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his ife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same \add is\add* Hebron in the land of Canaan.
And the field, and the cave that \add is\add* therein, ere made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth.
And Abraham as old, \add and\add* ell stricken in age: and the \sc Lord\sc* had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
and I ill make thee sear by the \sc Lord\sc*, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a ife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, amongst hom I dell:
but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a ife unto my son Isaac.
And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the oman ill not be illing to follo me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from hence thou camest?
And Abraham said unto him, Beare thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

The \sc Lord\sc* God of heaven, hich took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and hich spake unto me, and that sare unto me, saying, Unto thy seed ill I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a ife unto my son from thence.
And if the oman ill not be illing to follo thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath: only bring not my son thither again.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sare to him concerning that matter.
And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master \add ere\add* in his hand: and he arose, and ent to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
And he made \add his\add* camels to kneel don ithout the city by a ell of ater at the time of the evening, \add even\add* the time that \add omen\add* go out to dra \add ater\add*.
And he said, O \sc Lord\sc* God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed \add this\add* day, and she kindness unto my master Abraham.
Behold, I stand \add here\add* by the ell of ater; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to dra ater:

and let it come to pass, \add that\add* the damsel to hom I shall say, Let don thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I ill give thy camels drink also: \add let the same be\add* she \add that\add* thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I kno that thou hast sheed kindness unto my master.
And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that behold, Rebekah came out, ho as born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the ife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, ith her pitcher upon her shoulder.
And the damsel \add as\add* very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man knon her: and she ent don to the ell, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little ater of thy pitcher.
And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let don her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
And hen she had done giving him drink, she said, I ill dra \add ater\add* for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the ell to dra \add ater\add*, and dre for all his camels.
And the man ondering at her held his peace, to it hether the \sc Lord\sc* had made his journey prosperous or not.
And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel eight, and to bracelets for her hands of ten \add shekels\add* eight of gold;
and said, Whose daughter \add art\add* thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room \add in\add* thy father’s house for us to lodge in?
And she said unto him, I \add am\add* the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, hich she bare unto Nahor.
She said moreover unto him, We have both stra and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
And the man boed don his head, and orshipped the \sc Lord\sc*.

And he said, Blessed \add be\add* the \sc Lord\sc* God of my master Abraham, ho hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I \add being\add* in the ay, the \sc Lord\sc* led me to the house of my master’s brethren.
And the damsel ran, and told \add them of\add* her mother’s house these things.
And Rebekah had a brother, and his name \add as\add* Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the ell.

And it came to pass, hen he sa the earring and bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and hen he heard the ords of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and behold, he stood by the camels at the ell.
And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the \sc Lord\sc*; herefore standest thou ithout? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
And the man came into the house: and he ungirded \add his\add* camels, and gave stra and provender for the camels, and ater to ash his feet, and the men’s feet that \add ere\add* ith him.
And there as set \add meat\add* before him to eat: but he said, I ill not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
And he said, I \add am\add* Abraham’s servant.
And the \sc Lord\sc* hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.
And Sarah my master’s ife bare a son to my master hen she as old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
And my master made me sear, saying, Thou shalt not take a ife to my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in hose land I dell:
but thou shalt go unto my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a ife unto my son.
And I said unto my master, Peradventure the oman ill not follo me.
And he said unto me, The \sc Lord\sc*, before hom I alk, ill send his angel ith thee, and prosper thy ay; and thou shalt take a ife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:
then shalt thou be clear from \add this\add* my oath, hen thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee \add one\add*, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
And I came this day unto the ell, and said, O \sc Lord\sc* God of my master Abraham, if no thou do prosper my ay hich I go:

behold, I stand by the ell of ater; and it shall come to pass, \add that hen\add* the virgin cometh forth to dra \add ater\add*, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little ater of thy pitcher to drink;

And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter \add art\add* thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, hom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.

And they said, We ill call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.

And they sent aay Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou \add art\add* our sister, be thou \add the mother\add* of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those hich hate them.
And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and folloed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and ent his ay.
And Isaac came from the ay of the ell Lahai-roi; for he delt in the south country.
And Isaac ent out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lift up his eyes, and sa, and behold, the camels \add ere\add* coming.
And Rebekah lift up her eyes, and hen she sa Isaac, she lighted off the camel.
For she had said unto the servant, What man \add is\add* this that alketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It \add is\add* my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his ife; and he loved her: and Isaac as comforted after his mother’s \add death\add*.
Then again Abraham took a ife, and her name \add as\add* Keturah.

And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan ere Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah. All these \add ere\add* the children of Keturah.

But unto the sons of the concubines, hich Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them aay from Isaac his son, hile he yet lived, eastard, unto the east country.
And these \add are\add* the days of the years of Abraham’s life hich he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.

And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, hich \add is\add* before Mamre;

No these \add are\add* the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, hom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham:

and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
these \add are\add* the sons of Ishmael, and these \add are\add* their names, by their tons, and by their castles; telve princes according to their nations.
And these \add are\add* the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and as gathered unto his people.
And they delt from Havilah unto Shur, that \add is\add* before Egypt, as thou goest toards Assyria: \add and\add* he died in the presence of all his brethren.
And these \add are\add* the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begat Isaac:

And there as a famine in the land, besides the first famine that as in the days of Abraham. And Isaac ent unto Abimelech king of the Philistims unto Gerar.

sojourn in this land, and I ill be ith thee, and ill bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I ill give all these countries, and I ill perform the oath hich I sare unto Abraham thy father;
and I ill make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and ill give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;

and the men of the place asked \add him\add* of his ife; and he said, She \add is\add* my sister: for he feared to say, \add She is\add* my ife; lest, \add said he\add*, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she \add as\add* fair to look upon.

And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, No \add this\add* time ill my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore as his name called Levi.
And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, No ill I praise the \sc Lord\sc*: therefore she called his name Judah; and left bearing.
And hen Rachel sa that she bare Jacob no \add children\add*, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
And Jacob’s anger as kindled against Rachel: and he said, \add Am\add* I in God’s stead, ho hath ithheld from thee the fruit of the omb?
And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.
And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to ife: and Jacob ent in unto her.
And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.

And \add that\add* food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, hich shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.
And the thing as good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can e find \add such a one\add* as this \add is\add*, a man in hom the spirit of God \add is?\add*
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath sheed thee all this, \add there is\add* none so discreet and ise as thou \add art:\add*
thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy ord shall all my people be ruled: only \add in\add* the throne ill I be greater than thou.

And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell unto them; saying,
The man, \add ho is\add* the lord of the land, spake roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.

And their father Israel said unto them, If \add it must be\add* so no, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry don the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:
and take double money in your hand; and the money that as brought again in the mouth of your sacks, carry \add it\add* again in your hand; peradventure it \add as\add* an oversight:
take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:
and God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send aay your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.
And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and ent don \add to\add* Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

And the men ere afraid, because they ere brought into Joseph’s house; and they said, Because of the money that as returned in our sacks at the first time \add are\add* e brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.

and said, O sir, e came indeed don at the first time to buy food:

and it came to pass, hen e came to the inn, that e opened our sacks, and behold, every man’s money \add as\add* in the mouth of his sack, our money in full eight: and e have brought it again in our hand.
And other money have e brought don in our hands to buy food: e cannot tell ho put our money in our sacks.

And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, hich did eat ith him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread ith the Hebres, for that \add is\add* an abomination unto the Egyptians.

\add And\add* hen they ere gone out of the city, \add and\add* not \add yet\add* far off, Joseph said unto his steard, Up, follo after the men; and hen thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rearded evil for good?
\add Is\add* not this \add it\add* in hich my lord drinketh, and hereby indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in \add so\add* doing.

And they said unto him, Wherefore saith my lord these ords? God forbid that thy servants should do according to this thing:

With hom\add soever\add* of thy servants it be found, both let him die, and e also ill be my lord’s bondmen.

Then Judah came near unto him, and said, O my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a ord in my lord’s ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant: for thou \add art\add* even as Pharaoh.

Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man ith him, hile Joseph made himself knon unto his brethren.

And he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck, and ept; and Benjamin ept upon his neck.

And they took their cattle, and their goods, hich they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed ith him:
his sons, and his sons’ sons ith him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and all his seed brought he ith him into Egypt.

The sons of Rachel Jacob’s ife; Joseph, and Benjamin.

and the sons of Joseph, hich ere born him in Egypt, \add ere\add* to souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, hich came into Egypt, \add ere\add* threescore and ten.

And Joseph said unto his brethren, and unto his father’s house, I ill go up, and she Pharaoh, and say unto him, My brethren, and my father’s house, hich \add ere\add* in the land of Canaan, are come unto me;
and the men \add are\add* shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.

the land of Egypt \add is\add* before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dell; in the land of Goshen let them dell: and if thou knoest \add any\add* man of activity amongst them, then make them rulers over my cattle.

When that year as ended, they came unto him the second year, and said unto him, We ill not hide \add it\add* from my lord, ho that our money is spent; my lord also had our herds of cattle; there is not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:

herefore shall e die before thine eyes, both e and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and e and our land ill be servants unto Pharaoh: and give \add us\add* seed, that e may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate.
And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them: so the land became Pharaoh’s.

Only the land of the priests bought he not; for the priests had a portion assigned them of Pharaoh, and did eat their portion hich Pharaoh gave them: herefore they sold not their lands.
Then Joseph said unto the people, Behold, I have bought you \add this\add* day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, \add here is\add* seed for you, and ye shall so the land.

And it shall come to pass in the increase, that you shall give the fifth \add part\add* unto Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your on, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace in the sight of my lord, and e ill be Pharaoh’s servants.
And Joseph made it a la over the land of Egypt unto this day, \add that\add* Pharaoh should have the fifth \add part;\add* except the land of the priests only, \add hich\add* became not Pharaoh’s.
