And make one cherub on the one end, and the other cherub on the other end: \add even\add* of the mercy seat shall ye make the cherubims on the to ends thereof.

And the cherubims shall stretch forth \add their\add* ings on high, covering the mercy seat ith their ings, and their faces \add shall look\add* one to another; toard the mercy seat shall the faces of the cherubims be.
And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the Testimony that I shall give thee.

And there I ill meet ith thee, and I ill commune ith thee from above the mercy seat, from beteen the to cherubims hich \add are\add* upon the ark of the Testimony, of all \add things\add* hich I ill give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.
Thou shalt also make a table \add of\add* shittim ood: to cubits \add shall be\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
And thou shalt overlay it ith pure gold, and make thereto a cron \add of\add* gold round about.
And thou shalt make unto it a border of a handbreadth round about, and thou shalt make a golden cron to the border thereof round about.
And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that \add are\add* on the four feet thereof.
Over against the border shall the rings be for places of the staves to bear the table.
And thou shalt make the staves \add of\add* shittim ood, and overlay them ith gold, that the table may be borne ith them.
And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and spoons thereof, and covers thereof, and bols thereof, to cover ithal: \add of\add* pure gold shalt thou make them.
And thou shalt set upon the table shebread before me alay.
And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: \add of\add* beaten ork shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bols, his knops, and his floers, shall be of the same.
And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side:

three bols made like unto almonds, \add ith\add* a knop and a floer in one branch; and three bols made like almonds in the other branch, \add ith\add* a knop and a floer: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick.
And in the candlestick \add shall be\add* four bols made like unto almonds, \add ith\add* their knops and their floers.

And \add there shall be\add* a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick.
Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it \add shall be\add* one beaten ork \add of\add* pure gold.
And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.
And the tongs thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, \add shall be of\add* pure gold.
\add Of\add* a talent of pure gold shall he make it, ith all these vessels.
And look that thou make \add them\add* after their pattern, hich as sheed thee in the mount.

Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle \add ith\add* ten curtains \add of\add* fine tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: \add ith\add* cherubims \add of\add* cunning ork shalt thou make them.
The length of one curtain \add shall be\add* eight and tenty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: \add and\add* every one of the curtains shall have one measure.
The five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and \add other\add* five curtains \add shall be\add* coupled one to another.

And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likeise shalt thou make in the uttermost edge of \add another\add* curtain, in the coupling of the second.

Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that \add is\add* in the coupling of the second; that the loops may take hold one of another.
And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains together ith the taches: and it shall be one tabernacle.
And thou shalt make curtains \add of\add* goats’ \add hair\add* to be a covering upon the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make.
The length of one curtain \add shall be\add* thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: \add and\add* the eleven curtains \add shall be all\add* of one measure.
And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.
And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain \add that is\add* outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops in the edge of the curtain hich coupleth the second.
And thou shalt make fifty taches of brass, and put the taches into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
And the remnant that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the backside of the tabernacle.

And a cubit on the one side, and a cubit on the other side of that hich remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, it shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
And thou shalt make a covering for the tent \add of\add* rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering above of badgers’ skins.
And thou shalt make boards for the tabernacle \add of\add* shittim ood standing up.
Ten cubits \add shall be\add* the length of a board, and a cubit and a half \add shall be\add* the breadth of one board.
To tenons \add shall there be\add* in one board, set in order one against another: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, tenty boards on the south side southard.
And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the tenty boards; to sockets under one board for his to tenons, and to sockets under another board for his to tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle on the north side \add there shall be\add* tenty boards:
and their forty sockets \add of\add* silver; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And for the sides of the tabernacle estard thou shalt make six boards.
And to boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the to sides.
And they shall be coupled together beneath, and they shall be coupled together above the head of it unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the to corners.
And they shall be eight boards, and their sockets \add of\add* silver, sixteen sockets; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And thou shalt make bars \add of\add* shittim ood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the to sides estard.
And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall reach from end to end.
And thou shalt overlay the boards ith gold, and make their rings \add of\add* gold \add for\add* places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars ith gold.
And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof hich as sheed thee in the mount.
And thou shalt make a vail \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen \add of\add* cunning ork: \add ith\add* cherubims shall it be made:
and thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of shittim \add ood\add* overlaid ith gold: their hooks \add shall be of\add* gold, upon the four sockets of silver.

And thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches, that thou mayest bring in thither ithin the vail the ark of the Testimony: and the vail shall divide unto you beteen the holy \add place\add* and the most holy.
And thou shalt put the mercy seat upon the ark of the Testimony in the most holy \add place\add*.
And thou shalt set the table ithout the vail, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toard the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.
And thou shalt make a hanging for the door of the tent, \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, rought ith needleork.

And thou shalt make for the hanging five pillars of shittim \add ood\add*, and overlay them ith gold, \add and\add* their hooks \add shall be of\add* gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.
And thou shalt make an altar \add of\add* shittim ood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height thereof \add shall be\add* three cubits.
And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof: his horns shall be of the same: and thou shalt overlay it ith brass.
And thou shalt make his pans to receive his ashes, and his shovels, and his basons, and his fleshhooks, and his firepans: all the vessels thereof thou shalt make \add of\add* brass.
And thou shalt make for it a grate of netork \add of\add* brass; and upon the net shalt thou make four brasen rings in the four corners thereof.
And thou shalt put it under the compass of the altar beneath, that the net may be even to the midst of the altar.
And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of shittim ood, and overlay them ith brass.
And the staves shall be put into the rings, and the staves shall be upon the to sides of the altar, to bear it.
Hollo ith boards shalt thou make it: as it as sheed thee in the mount, so shall they make \add it\add*.
And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southard \add there shall be\add* hangings for the court \add of\add* fine tined linen of an hundred cubits long for one side:
and the tenty pillars thereof and their tenty sockets \add shall be of\add* brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add shall be of\add* silver.

And likeise for the north side in length \add there shall be\add* hangings of an hundred \add cubits\add* long, and his tenty pillars and their tenty sockets \add of\add* brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add* silver.
And \add for\add* the breadth of the court on the est side \add shall be\add* hangings of fifty cubits: their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
And the breadth of the court on the east side eastard \add shall be\add* fifty cubits.
The hangings of \add one\add* side \add of the gate shall be\add* fifteen cubits: their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And on the other side \add shall be\add* hangings, fifteen \add cubits:\add* their pillars three, and their sockets three.

And for the gate of the court \add shall be\add* a hanging of tenty cubits, \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, rought ith needleork: \add and\add* their pillars \add shall be\add* four, and their sockets four.
All the pillars round about the court \add shall be\add* filleted \add ith\add* silver; their hooks \add shall be of\add* silver, and their sockets \add of\add* brass.
The length of the court \add shall be\add* an hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every here, and the height five cubits \add of\add* fine tined linen, and their sockets \add of\add* brass.
All the vessels of the tabernacle in all the service thereof, and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, \add shall be of\add* brass.
And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn alays.

In the tabernacle of the congregation ithout the vail, hich \add is\add* before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the \sc Lord\sc*: \add it shall be\add* a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.

And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons ith him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office, \add even\add* Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for glory and for beauty.

And thou shalt speak unto all \add that are\add* ise hearted, hom I have filled ith the spirit of isdom, that they may make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

And these \add are\add* the garments hich they shall make; a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.
And they shall make the ephod \add of\add* gold, \add of\add* blue, and \add of\add* purple, \add of\add* scarlet, and fine tined linen, \add ith\add* cunning ork.
It shall have the to shoulderpieces \add thereof\add* joined at the to edges thereof; and \add so\add* it shall be joined together.

And the curious girdle of the ephod, hich \add is\add* upon it, shall be of the same, according to the ork thereof; \add even of\add* gold, \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
And thou shalt take to onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:
six of their names on one stone, and the \add other\add* six names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth.

\add With\add* the ork of an engraver in stone, \add like\add* the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the to stones ith the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set \add in\add* ouches \add of\add* gold.

And thou shalt put the to stones upon the shoulders of the ephod \add for\add* stones of memorial unto the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before the \sc Lord\sc* upon his to shoulders for a memorial.
And thou shalt make ouches \add of\add* gold;
and to chains \add of\add* pure gold at the ends; \add of\add* reathen ork shalt thou make them, and fasten the reathen chains to the ouches.

And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment \add ith\add* cunning ork; after the ork of the ephod thou shalt make it; \add of\add* gold, \add of\add* blue, and \add of\add* purple, and \add of\add* scarlet, and \add of\add* fine tined linen, shalt thou make it.
Foursquare it shall be \add being\add* doubled; a span \add shall be\add* the length thereof, and a span \add shall be\add* the breadth thereof.
And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, \add even\add* four ros of stones: \add the first\add* ro \add shall be\add* a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this \add shall be\add* the first ro.
And the second ro \add shall be\add* an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
And the third ro a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
And the fourth ro a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings.

And the stones shall be ith the names of the children of Israel, telve, according to their names, \add like\add* the engravings of a signet; every one ith his name shall they be according to the telve tribes.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate chains at the ends \add of\add* reathen ork \add of\add* pure gold.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate to rings of gold, and shalt put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate.
And thou shalt put the to reathen \add chains of\add* gold in the to rings \add hich are\add* on the ends of the breastplate.
And \add the other\add* to ends of the to reathen \add chains\add* thou shalt fasten in the to ouches, and put \add them\add* on the shoulderpieces of the ephod before it.
And thou shalt make to rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the to ends of the breastplate in the border thereof, hich \add is\add* in the side of the ephod inard.

And to \add other\add* rings of gold thou shalt make, and shalt put them on the to sides of the ephod underneath, toards the forepart thereof, over against \add the other\add* coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod.

And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod ith a lace of blue, that \add it\add* may be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.

And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, hen he goeth in unto the holy \add place\add*, for a memorial before the \sc Lord\sc* continually.

And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, hen he goeth in before the \sc Lord\sc*: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the \sc Lord\sc* continually.
And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
And there shall be a hole in the top of it, in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of oven ork round about the hole of it, as it ere the hole of an habergeon, \add that\add* it be not rent.
And \add beneath\add* upon the hem of it thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, round about the hem thereof; and bells of gold beteen them round about:
a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe round about.
And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and his sound shall be heard hen he goeth in unto the holy \add place\add* before the \sc Lord\sc*, and hen he cometh out, that he die not.
And thou shalt make a plate \add of\add* pure gold, and grave upon it, \add like\add* the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
And thou shalt put it on a blue lace, that it may be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.

And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy \add things\add*, hich the children of Israel shall hallo in all their holy gifts; and it shall be alays upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the \sc Lord\sc*.
And thou shalt embroider the coat of fine linen, and thou shalt make the mitre \add of\add* fine linen, and thou shalt make the girdle \add of\add* needleork.
And for Aaron’s sons thou shalt make coats, and thou shalt make for them girdles, and bonnets shalt thou make for them, for glory and for beauty.
And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and his sons ith him; and shalt anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover \add their\add* nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

and they shall be upon Aaron, and upon his sons, hen they come in unto the tabernacle of the congregation, or hen they come near unto the altar to minister in the holy \add place;\add* that they bear not iniquity, and die: \add it shall be\add* a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him.
And this \add is\add* the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallo them, to minister unto me in the priest’s office: Take one young bullock, and to rams ithout blemish,
and unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered ith oil, and afers unleavened anointed ith oil: \add of\add* heaten flour shalt thou make them.
And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, ith the bullock and the to rams.
And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and shalt ash them ith ater.
And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him ith the curious girdle of the ephod:
and thou shalt put the mitre upon his head, and put the holy cron upon the mitre.
Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour \add it\add* upon his head, and anoint him.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.

And thou shalt gird them \add ith\add* girdles, Aaron and his sons, and put the bonnets on them: and the priest’s office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.
And thou shalt cause a bullock to be brought before the tabernacle of the congregation: and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the bullock.
And thou shalt kill the bullock before the \sc Lord\sc*, \add by\add* the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and put \add it\add* upon the horns of the altar ith thy finger, and pour all the blood beside the bottom of the altar.

And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inards, and the caul \add that is\add* above the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat that \add is\add* upon them, and burn \add them\add* upon the altar.
But the flesh of the bullock, and his skin, and his dung, shalt thou burn ith fire ithout the camp: it \add is\add* a sin offering.
Thou shalt also take one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.
And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take his blood, and sprinkle \add it\add* round about upon the altar.
And thou shalt cut the ram in pieces, and ash the inards of him, and his legs, and put \add them\add* unto his pieces, and unto his head.
And thou shalt burn the hole ram upon the altar: it \add is\add* a burnt offering unto the \sc Lord\sc*: it \add is\add* a seet savour, an offering made by fire unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.

Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put \add it\add* upon the tip of the \add right\add* ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

And thou shalt take of the blood that \add is\add* upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle \add it\add* upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons ith him: and he shall be halloed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments ith him.

Also thou shalt take of the ram the fat and the rump, and the fat that covereth the inards, and the caul \add above\add* the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat that \add is\add* upon them, and the right shoulder; for it \add is\add* a ram of consecration:
and one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one afer out of the basket of the unleavened bread that \add is\add* before the \sc Lord\sc*:
and thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt ave them \add for\add* a ave offering before the \sc Lord\sc*.

And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn \add them\add* upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a seet savour before the \sc Lord\sc*: it \add is\add* an offering made by fire unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s consecrations, and ave it \add for\add* a ave offering before the \sc Lord\sc*: and it shall be thy part.

And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the ave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, hich is aved, and hich is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, \add even\add* of \add that\add* hich \add is\add* for Aaron, and of \add that\add* hich \add is\add* for his sons:

and it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’ by a statute for ever from the children of Israel: for it \add is\add* a heave offering: and it shall be a heave offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifice of their peace offerings, \add even\add* their heave offering unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And the holy garments of Aaron shall be his sons’ after him, to be anointed therein, and to be consecrated in them.
\add And\add* that son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days, hen he cometh into the tabernacle of the congregation to minister in the holy \add place\add*.
And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seethe his flesh in the holy place.
And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that \add is\add* in the basket, \add by\add* the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And they shall eat those \add things\add* hereith the atonement as made, to consecrate \add and\add* to sanctify them: but a stranger shall not eat \add thereof\add*, because they \add are\add* holy.
And if \add ought\add* of the flesh of the consecrations, or of the bread, remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the remainder ith fire: it shall not be eaten, because it \add is\add* holy.
And thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all \add things\add* hich I have commanded thee: seven days shalt thou consecrate them.

And thou shalt offer every day a bullock \add for\add* a sin offering for atonement: and thou shalt cleanse the altar, hen thou hast made an atonement for it, and thou shalt anoint it, to sanctify it.
Seven days thou shalt make an atonement for the altar, and sanctify it; and it shall be an altar most holy: hatsoever toucheth the altar shall be holy.
No this \add is that\add* hich thou shalt offer upon the altar; to lambs of the first year day by day continually.
The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at even:
and ith the one lamb a tenth deal of flour mingled ith the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil; and the fourth \add part\add* of a hin of ine \add for\add* a drink offering.

And the other lamb thou shalt offer at even, \add and\add* shalt do thereto according to the meat offering of the morning, and according to the drink offering thereof, for a seet savour, an offering made by fire unto the \sc Lord\sc*.

\add This shall be\add* a continual burnt offering throughout your generations \add at\add* the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the \sc Lord\sc*: here I ill meet you, to speak there unto thee.
And there I ill meet ith the children of Israel, and \add the tabernacle\add* shall be sanctified by my glory.
And I ill sanctify the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar: I ill sanctify also both Aaron and his sons, to minister to me in the priest’s office.
And I ill dell amongst the children of Israel, and ill be their God.
And they shall kno that I \add am\add* the \sc Lord\sc* their God, that brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, that I may dell amongst them: I \add am\add* the \sc Lord\sc* their God.
And thou shalt make an altar to burn incense upon: \add of\add* shittim ood shalt thou make it.

A cubit \add shall be\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof; foursquare shall it be: and to cubits \add shall be\add* the height thereof: the horns thereof \add shall be\add* of the same.
And thou shalt overlay it ith pure gold, the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns thereof; and thou shalt make unto it a cron \add of\add* gold round about.

And to golden rings shalt thou make to it under the cron of it, by the to corners thereof, upon the to sides of it shalt thou make \add it;\add* and they shall be for places for the staves to bear it ithal.
And thou shalt make the staves \add of\add* shittim ood, and overlay them ith gold.
And thou shalt put it before the vail that \add is\add* by the ark of the Testimony, before the mercy seat that \add is\add* over the Testimony, here I ill meet ith thee.
And Aaron shall burn thereon seet incense every morning: hen he dresseth the lamps, he shall burn incense upon it.
And hen Aaron lighteth the lamps at even, he shall burn incense upon it, a perpetual incense before the \sc Lord\sc* throughout your generations.
Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon, nor burnt sacrifice, nor meat offering; neither shall ye pour drink offering thereon.

And Aaron shall make an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year ith the blood of the sin offering of atonements: once in the year shall he make atonement upon it throughout your generations: it \add is\add* most holy unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And the \sc Lord\sc* spake unto Moses, saying,

And he made curtains \add of\add* goats’ \add hair\add* for the tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains he made them.
The length of one curtain \add as\add* thirty cubits, and four cubits \add as\add* the breadth of one curtain: the eleven curtains \add ere\add* of one size.
And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
And he made fifty loops upon the uttermost edge of the curtain in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain hich coupleth the second.
And he made fifty taches of brass to couple the tent together, that \add it\add* might be one.
And he made a covering for the tent \add of\add* rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers’ skins above \add that\add*.
And he made boards for the tabernacle \add of\add* shittim ood, standing up.
The length of a board \add as\add* ten cubits, and the breadth of a board one cubit and a half.
One board had to tenons, equally distant one from another: thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And he made boards for the tabernacle; tenty boards for the south side southard:
and forty sockets of silver he made under the tenty boards; to sockets under one board for his to tenons, and to sockets under another board for his to tenons.
And for the other side of the tabernacle, \add hich is\add* toard the north corner, he made tenty boards,
and their forty sockets \add of\add* silver; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And for the sides of the tabernacle estard he made six boards.
And to boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the to sides.
And they ere coupled beneath, and coupled together at the head thereof, to one ring: thus he did to both of them in both the corners.
And there ere eight boards; and their sockets \add ere\add* sixteen sockets \add of\add* silver, under every board to sockets.
And he made bars of shittim ood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the sides estard.
And he made the middle bar to shoot through the boards from the one end to the other.
And he overlaid the boards ith gold, and made their rings \add of\add* gold \add to be\add* places for the bars, and overlaid the bars ith gold.
And he made a vail \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen: \add ith\add* cherubims made he it \add of\add* cunning ork.
And he made thereunto four pillars of shittim \add ood\add*, and overlaid them ith gold: their hooks \add ere of\add* gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.
And he made a hanging for the tabernacle door \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, \add of\add* needleork;
and the five pillars of it ith their hooks: and he overlaid their chapiters and their fillets ith gold: but their five sockets \add ere of\add* brass.
And Bezaleel made the ark \add of\add* shittim ood: to cubits and a half \add as\add* the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it:
and he overlaid it ith pure gold ithin and ithout, and made a cron \add of\add* gold to it round about.
And he cast for it four rings of gold, \add to be set\add* by the four corners of it; even to rings upon the one side of it, and to rings upon the other side of it.
And he made staves of shittim ood, and overlaid them ith gold.
And he put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
And he made the mercy seat \add of\add* pure gold: to cubits and a half \add as\add* the length thereof, and one cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
And he made to cherubims \add of\add* gold, beaten out of one piece made he them, on the to ends of the mercy seat;
one cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the \add other\add* end on that side: out of the mercy seat made he the cherubims on the to ends thereof.

And the cherubims spread out \add their\add* ings on high, \add and\add* covered ith their ings over the mercy seat, ith their faces one to another; \add even\add* to the mercy seatard ere the faces of the cherubims.
And he made the table \add of\add* shittim ood: to cubits \add as\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof:
and he overlaid it ith pure gold, and made thereunto a cron \add of\add* gold round about.
Also he made thereunto a border of a handbreadth round about; and made a cron of gold for the border thereof round about.
And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings upon the four corners that \add ere\add* in the four feet thereof.
Over against the border ere the rings, the places for the staves to bear the table.
And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim ood, and overlaid them ith gold, to bear the table.
And he made the vessels hich \add ere\add* upon the table, his dishes, and his spoons, and his bols, and \add his\add* covers to cover ithal, \add of\add* pure gold.
And he made the candlestick \add of\add* pure gold: \add of\add* beaten ork made he the candlestick; his shaft, and his branch, his bols, his knops, and his floers, ere of the same:
and six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

three bols made after the fashion of almonds in one branch, a knop and a floer; and three bols made like almonds in another branch, a knop and a floer: so throughout the six branches going out of the candlestick.
And in the candlestick \add ere\add* four bols made like almonds, his knops, and his floers:
and a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, and a knop under to branches of the same, according to the six branches going out of it.
Their knops and their branches ere of the same: all of it \add as\add* one beaten ork \add of\add* pure gold.
And he made his seven lamps, and his snuffers, and his snuffdishes, \add of\add* pure gold.
\add Of\add* a talent \add of\add* pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof.

And he made the incense altar \add of\add* shittim ood: the length of it \add as\add* a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit; \add it as\add* foursquare; and to cubits \add as\add* the height of it; the horns thereof ere of the same.
And he overlaid it ith pure gold, \add both\add* the top of it, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: also he made unto it a cron \add of\add* gold round about.
And he made to rings of gold for it under the cron thereof, by the to corners of it, upon the to sides thereof, to be places for the staves to bear it ithal.
And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim ood, and overlaid them ith gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of seet spices, \add according to\add* the ork of the apothecary.

And he made the altar of burnt offering \add of\add* shittim ood: five cubits \add as\add* the length thereof, and five cubits the breadth thereof; \add it as\add* foursquare; and three cubits the height thereof.
And he made the horns thereof on the four corners of it; the horns thereof ere of the same: and he overlaid it ith brass.
And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the basons, \add and\add* the fleshhooks, and the firepans: all the vessels thereof made he \add of\add* brass.
And he made for the altar a brasen grate of netork under the compass thereof beneath unto the midst of it.
And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grate of brass, \add to be\add* places for the staves.
And he made the staves \add of\add* shittim ood, and overlaid them ith brass.
And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar, to bear it ithal; he made \add the altar\add* hollo ith boards.

And he made the laver \add of\add* brass, and the foot of it \add of\add* brass, of the looking-glasses of \add the omen\add* assembling, hich assembled \add at\add* the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And he made the court: on the south side southard the hangings of the court \add ere of\add* fine tined linen, an hundred cubits:
their pillars \add ere\add* tenty, and their brasen sockets tenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add ere of\add* silver.

And for the north side \add the hangings ere\add* an hundred cubits, their pillars \add ere\add* tenty, and their sockets \add of\add* brass tenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add* silver.
And for the est side \add ere\add* hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add* silver.
And for the east side eastard fifty cubits.
The hangings of the \add one\add* side \add of the gate ere\add* fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And for the other side of the court gate, on this hand and that hand, \add ere\add* hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
All the hangings of the court round about \add ere of\add* fine tined linen.

And the sockets for the pillars \add ere of\add* brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add of\add* silver; and the overlaying of their chapiters \add of\add* silver; and all the pillars of the court \add ere\add* filleted \add ith\add* silver.

And the hanging for the gate of the court \add as\add* needleork, \add of\add* blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen: and tenty cubits \add as\add* the length, and the height in the breadth \add as\add* five cubits, anserable to the hangings of the court.
And their pillars \add ere\add* four, and their sockets \add of\add* brass four; their hooks \add of\add* silver, and the overlaying of their chapiters and their fillets \add of\add* silver.
And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round about, \add ere of\add* brass.

This is the sum of the tabernacle, \add even\add* of the tabernacle of Testimony, as it as counted, according to the commandment of Moses, \add for\add* the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son to Aaron the priest.
And Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And ith him \add as\add* Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a cunning orkman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen.

All the gold that as occupied for the ork in all the ork of the holy \add place\add*, even the gold of the offering, as tenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
And the silver of them that ere numbered of the congregation \add as\add* an hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and threescore and fifteen shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:

a bekah for every man, \add that is\add*, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that ent to be numbered, from tenty years old and upard, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty \add men\add*.
And of the hundred talents of silver ere cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail; an hundred sockets of the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five \add shekels\add* he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their chapiters, and filleted them.
And the brass of the offering \add as\add* seventy talents, and to thousand and four hundred shekels.
And thereith he made the sockets to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the brasen altar, and the brasen grate for it, and all the vessels of the altar,
and the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the court gate, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.
And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made clothes of service, to do service in the holy \add place\add*, and made the holy garments for Aaron; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he made the ephod \add of\add* gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut \add it into\add* ires, to ork \add it\add* in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, \add ith\add* cunning ork.
They made shoulderpieces for it, to couple \add it\add* together: by the to edges as it coupled together.

And the curious girdle of his ephod, that \add as\add* upon it, \add as\add* of the same, according to the ork thereof; \add of\add* gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And they rought onyx stones inclosed \add in\add* ouches \add of\add* gold, graven \add as\add* signets are graven, ith the names of the children of Israel.
And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, \add that they should be\add* stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he made the breastplate \add of\add* cunning ork, like the ork of the ephod; \add of\add* gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
It as foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span \add as\add* the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, \add being\add* doubled.
And they set in it four ros of stones: \add the first\add* ro \add as\add* a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: \add this as\add* the first ro.
And the second ro, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
And the third ro, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
And the fourth ro, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: \add they ere\add* inclosed \add in\add* ouches \add of\add* gold in their inclosings.

And the stones \add ere\add* according to the names of the children of Israel, telve, according to their names, \add like\add* the engravings of a signet, every one ith his name, according to the telve tribes.
And they made upon the breastplate chains at the ends, \add of\add* reathen ork \add of\add* pure gold.
And they made to ouches \add of\add* gold, and to gold rings; and put the to rings in the to ends of the breastplate.
And they put the to reathen \add chains of\add* gold in the to rings on the ends of the breastplate.
And the to ends of the to reathen \add chains\add* they fastened in the to ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod, before it.
And they made to rings of gold, and put \add them\add* on the to ends of the breastplate, upon the border of it, hich \add as\add* on the side of the ephod inard.

And they made to \add other\add* golden rings, and put them on the to sides of the ephod underneath, toard the forepart of it, over against the \add other\add* coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod.

And they did bind the breastplate by his rings unto the rings of the ephod ith a lace of blue, that \add it\add* might be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed from the ephod; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he made the robe of the ephod \add of\add* oven ork, all of blue.
And \add there as\add* a hole in the midst of the robe, as the hole of an habergeon, \add ith\add* a band round about the hole, \add that\add* it should not rend.
And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, \add and\add* tined \add linen\add*.
And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells beteen the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, round about beteen the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister \add in;\add* as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And they made coats \add of\add* fine linen \add of\add* oven ork for Aaron, and for his sons,
and a mitre \add of\add* fine linen, and goodly bonnets \add of\add* fine linen, and linen breeches \add of\add* fine tined linen,
and a girdle \add of\add* fine tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, \add of\add* needleork; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And they made the plate of the holy cron \add of\add* pure gold, and rote upon it a riting, \add like to\add* the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten \add it\add* on high upon the mitre; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
Thus as all the ork of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses, so did they.
And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all his furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his sockets,
and the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and the covering of badgers’ skins, and the vail of the covering,
the ark of the Testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy seat,
the table, \add and\add* all the vessels thereof, and the shebread,
the pure candlestick, \add ith\add* the lamps thereof, \add even ith\add* the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for light,
and the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the seet incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle door,
the brasen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver and his foot,

the hangings of the court, his pillars, and his sockets, and the hanging for the court gate, his cords, and his pins, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the congregation,
the clothes of service to do service in the holy \add place\add*, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons’ garments, to minister in the priest’s office.
According to all that the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the ork.
And Moses did look upon all the ork, and behold, they had done it as the \sc Lord\sc* had commanded, \add even\add* so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
And the \sc Lord\sc* spake unto Moses, saying,
On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
And thou shalt put therein the ark of the Testimony, and cover the ark ith the vail.
And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are to be set in order upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light the lamps thereof.
And thou shalt set the altar of gold for the incense before the ark of the Testimony, and put the hanging of the door to the tabernacle.
And thou shalt set the altar of the burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
And thou shalt set the laver beteen the tent of the congregation and the altar, and shalt put ater therein.
And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the hanging at the court gate.
And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that \add is\add* therein, and shalt hallo it, and all the vessels thereof: and it shall be holy.
And thou shalt anoint the altar of the burnt offering, and all his vessels, and sanctify the altar: and it shall be an altar most holy.
And thou shalt anoint the laver and his foot, and sanctify it.
And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and ash them ith ater.
And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them ith coats:

and thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
Thus did Moses: according to all that the \sc Lord\sc* commanded him, so did he.
And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first \add day\add* of the month, \add that\add* the tabernacle as reared up.
And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened his sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up his pillars.
And he spread abroad the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he took and put the Testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the mercy seat above upon the ark:
and he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the vail of the covering, and covered the ark of the Testimony; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he put the table in the tent of the congregation, upon the side of the tabernacle northard, ithout the vail.
And he set the bread in order upon it before the \sc Lord\sc*; as the \sc Lord\sc* had commanded Moses.
And he put the candlestick in the tent of the congregation, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southard.
And he lighted the lamps before the \sc Lord\sc*; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he put the golden altar in the tent of the congregation before the vail:
and he burnt seet incense thereon; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he set up the hanging at the door of the tabernacle.

And he put the altar of burnt offering \add by\add* the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the meat offering; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he set the laver beteen the tent of the congregation and the altar, and put ater there, to ash \add ithal\add*.
And Moses and Aaron and his sons ashed their hands and their feet thereat:
hen they ent into the tent of the congregation, and hen they came near unto the altar, they ashed; as the \sc Lord\sc* commanded Moses.
And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the hanging of the court gate. So Moses finished the ork.
Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the \sc Lord\sc* filled the tabernacle.
And Moses as not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the \sc Lord\sc* filled the tabernacle.
And hen the cloud as taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel ent onard in all their journeys:
but if the cloud ere not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it as taken up.
For the cloud of the \sc Lord\sc* \add as\add* upon the tabernacle by day, and fire as on it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
\sc And\sc* the \sc Lord\sc* called unto Moses, and spake unto him out of the tabernacle of the congregation, saying,

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If \add any\add* man of you bring an offering unto the \sc Lord\sc*, ye shall bring your offering of the cattle, \add even\add* of the herd, and of the flock.

If his offering \add be\add* a burnt sacrifice of the herd, let him offer a male ithout blemish: he shall offer it of his on voluntary ill at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the \sc Lord\sc*.
And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

And he shall kill the bullock before the \sc Lord\sc*: and the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall bring the blood, and sprinkle the blood round about upon the altar that \add is by\add* the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And he shall flay the burnt offering, and cut it into his pieces.
And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire upon the altar, and lay the ood in order upon the fire:
and the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall lay the parts, the head, and the fat, in order upon the ood that \add is\add* on the fire hich \add is\add* upon the altar:
but his inards and his legs shall he ash in ater: and the priest shall burn all on the altar, \add to be\add* a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a seet savour unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And if his offering \add be\add* of the flocks, \add namely\add*, of the sheep, or of the goats, for a burnt sacrifice; he shall bring it a male ithout blemish.
And he shall kill it on the side of the altar northard before the \sc Lord\sc*: and the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall sprinkle his blood round about upon the altar.
And he shall cut it into his pieces, ith his head and his fat: and the priest shall lay them in order on the ood that \add is\add* on the fire hich \add is\add* upon the altar:

but he shall ash the inards and the legs ith ater: and the priest shall bring \add it\add* all, and burn \add it\add* upon the altar: it \add is\add* a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a seet savour unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And if the burnt sacrifice for his offering to the \sc Lord\sc* \add be\add* of fols, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves, or of young pigeons.
And the priest shall bring it unto the altar, and ring off his head, and burn \add it\add* on the altar; and the blood thereof shall be rung out at the side of the altar:
and he shall pluck aay his crop ith his feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, by the place of the ashes:

and he shall cleave it ith the ings thereof, \add but\add* shall not divide \add it\add* asunder: and the priest shall burn it upon the altar, upon the ood that \add is\add* upon the fire: it \add is\add* a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a seet savour unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And hen any ill offer a meat offering unto the \sc Lord\sc*, his offering shall be \add of\add* fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon:

and he shall bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests: and he shall take thereout his handful of the flour thereof, and of the oil thereof, ith all the frankincense thereof; and the priest shall burn the memorial of it upon the altar, \add to be\add* an offering made by fire, of a seet savour unto the \sc Lord\sc*:
and the remnant of the meat offering \add shall be\add* Aaron’s and his sons’: \add it is a thing\add* most holy of the offerings of the \sc Lord\sc* made by fire.
And if thou bring an oblation of a meat offering baken in the oven, \add it shall be\add* unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled ith oil, or unleavened afers anointed ith oil.
And if thy oblation \add be\add* a meat offering \add baken\add* in a pan, it shall be \add of\add* fine flour unleavened, mingled ith oil.
Thou shalt part it in pieces, and pour oil thereon: it \add is\add* a meat offering.
And if thy oblation \add be\add* a meat offering \add baken\add* in the fryingpan, it shall be made \add of\add* fine flour ith oil.
And thou shalt bring the meat offering that is made of these \add things\add* unto the \sc Lord\sc*: and hen it is presented unto the priest, he shall bring it unto the altar.
And the priest shall take from the meat offering a memorial thereof, and shall burn \add it\add* upon the altar: \add it is\add* an offering made by fire, of a seet savour unto the \sc Lord\sc*.
And that hich is left of the meat offering \add shall be\add* Aaron’s and his sons’: \add it is\add* a thing most holy of the offerings of the \sc Lord\sc* made by fire.

No meat offering, hich ye shall bring unto the \sc Lord\sc*, shall be made \add ith\add* leaven: for ye shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, \add in\add* any offering of the \sc Lord\sc* made by fire.
\add As for\add* the oblation of the firstfruits, ye shall offer them unto the \sc Lord\sc*: but they shall not be burnt on the altar for a seet savour.

And every oblation of thy meat offering shalt thou season ith salt; neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy God to be lacking from thy meat offering: ith all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt.

And if thou offer a meat offering of \add thy\add* firstfruits unto the \sc Lord\sc*, thou shalt offer for the meat offering of thy firstfruits green ears of corn dried by the fire, \add even\add* corn beaten out of full ears.
And thou shalt put oil upon it, and lay frankincense thereon: it \add is\add* a meat offering.
