But in all this \add time\add* as not I at Jerusalem: for in the to and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the king, and after certain days obtained I \add leave\add* of the king:
and I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.
Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, ith the meat offering and the frankincense.
And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given \add them:\add* for the Levites and the singers, that did the ork, ere fled every one to his field.
Then contended I ith the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the ne ine and the oil unto the treasuries.

And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them \add as\add* Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah: for they ere counted faithful, and their office \add as\add* to distribute unto their brethren.
Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and ipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.

In those days sa I in Judah \add some\add* treading ine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also ine, grapes, and figs, and all \add manner of\add* burdens, hich they brought \add into\add* Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified \add against them\add* in the day herein they sold victuals.
There delt men of Tyre also therein, hich brought fish, and all \add manner of\add* are, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
Then I contended ith the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing \add is\add* this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
Did not your fathers thus, and \add did not\add* our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more rath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And it came to pass, that hen the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and \add some\add* of my servants set I at the gates, \add that\add* there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
So the merchants and sellers of all \add kind of\add* are lodged ithout Jerusalem once or tice.
Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the all? if ye do \add so\add* again, I ill lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no \add more\add* on the sabbath.

And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and \add that\add* they should come \add and\add* keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, \add concerning\add* this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.
In those days also sa I Jes \add that\add* had married ives of Ashdod, of Ammon, \add and\add* of Moab:
and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jes’ language, but according to the language of each people.

And I contended ith them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and pluckt off their hair, and made them sear by God, \add saying\add*, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these \add things?\add* yet among many nations as there no king like him, ho as beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: \add nevertheless\add* even him did outlandish omen cause to sin.
Shall e then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange ives?
And \add one\add* of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, \add as\add* son in la to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.
Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the ards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business;
and for the ood offering, at times appointed, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
\sc No\sc* it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this \add is\add* Ahasuerus hich reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia, \add over\add* an hundred and seven and tenty provinces:)
\add that\add* in those days, hen the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, hich \add as\add* in Shushan the palace,
in the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his princes and his servants; the poer of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces, \add being\add* before him:
hen he sheed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour of his excellent majesty many days, \add even\add* an hundred and fourscore days.

And hen these days ere expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that ere present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace;

\add here ere\add* hite, green, and blue \add hangings\add*, fastened ith cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble: the beds \add ere of\add* gold and silver, upon a pavement of red, and blue, and hite, and black marble.
And \add they\add* gave \add them\add* drink in vessels of gold, (the vessels being diverse one from another,) and royal ine in abundance, according to the state of the king.
And the drinking \add as\add* according to the la; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that \add they\add* should do according to every man’s pleasure.
Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the omen \add in\add* the royal house hich \add belonged\add* to king Ahasuerus.

On the seventh day, hen the heart of the king as merry ith ine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,
to bring Vashti the queen before the king ith the cron royal, to she the people and the princes her beauty: for she \add as\add* fair to look on.
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by \add his\add* chamberlains: therefore as the king very roth, and his anger burned in him.
Then the king said to the ise \add men,\add* hich kne the times, (for so \add as\add* the king’s manner toards all that kne la and judgment:

and the next unto him \add as\add* Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, \add and\add* Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, hich sa the king’s face, \add and\add* hich sat the first in the kingdom;)
What shall \add e\add* do unto the queen Vashti according to la, because she hath not performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?

And Memucan ansered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done rong to the king only, but \add also\add* to all the princes, and to all the people that \add are\add* in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.

For \add this\add* deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all omen, so that \add they\add* shall despise their husbands in their eyes, hen it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.
Likeise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king’s princes, hich have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus \add shall there arise\add* too much contempt and rath.

If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from him, and let it be ritten among the las of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no \add more\add* before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another \add that is\add* better than she.
And hen the king’s decree hich he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it \add is\add* great,) all the ives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.
And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the ord of Memucan:

for he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the riting thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his on house, and that it should be published according to the language of every people.
After these things, hen the rath of king Ahasuerus as appeased, he remembered Vashti, and hat she had done, and hat as decreed against her.
Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:

and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the omen, unto the custody of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the omen; and let their things for purification be given \add them:\add*
and let the maiden hich pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
\add No\add* in Shushan the palace there as a certain Je, hose name \add as\add* Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite;
ho had been carried aay from Jerusalem ith the captivity hich had been carried aay ith Jeconiah king of Judah, hom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried aay.

And he brought up Hadassah, that \add is\add*, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid \add as\add* fair and beautiful; hom Mordecai, hen her father and mother ere dead, took for his on daughter.

So it came to pass, hen the king’s commandment and his decree as heard, and hen many maidens ere gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther as brought \add also\add* unto the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the omen.

And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, ith such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, \add hich ere\add* meet to be given her, out of the king’s house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best \add place\add* of the house of the omen.
Esther had not sheed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not she \add it\add*.
And Mordecai alked every day before the court of the omen’s house, to kno ho Esther did, and hat should become of her.

No hen every maid’s turn as come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been telve months, according to the manner of the omen, (for so ere the days of their purifications accomplished, \add to it\add*, six months ith oil of myrrh, and six months ith seet odours, and ith \add other\add* things for the purifying of the omen;)
then thus came \add every\add* maiden unto the king; hatsoever she desired as given her to go ith her out of the house of the omen unto the king’s house.

In the evening she ent, and on the morro she returned into the second house of the omen, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s chamberlain, hich kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and \add that\add* she ere called by name.

No hen the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, ho had taken \add her\add* for his daughter, as come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but hat Hegai the king’s chamberlain, the keeper of the omen, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
So Esther as taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, hich \add is\add* the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

And the king loved Esther above all the omen, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal cron upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, \add even\add* Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.
And hen the virgins ere gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king’s gate.
Esther had not \add yet\add* sheed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as hen she as brought up ith him.
In those days, hile Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, to of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those hich kept the door, ere roth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
And the thing as knon to Mordecai, ho told \add it\add* unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king \add thereof\add* in Mordecai’s name.
And hen inquisition as made of the matter, it as found out; therefore they ere both hanged on a tree: and it as ritten in the book of the chronicles before the king.
After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that \add ere\add* ith him.
And all the king’s servants, that \add ere\add* in the king’s gate, boed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai boed not, nor did \add him\add* reverence.
Then the king’s servants, hich \add ere\add* in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
No it came to pass, hen they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see hether Mordecai’s matters ould stand: for he had told them that he \add as\add* a Je.
And hen Haman sa that Mordecai boed not, nor did him reverence, \add then\add* as Haman full \add of\add* rath.

And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had sheed him the people of Mordecai: herefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jes that \add ere\add* throughout the hole kingdom of Ahasuerus, \add even\add* the people of Mordecai.

In the first month, that \add is\add*, the month Nisan, in the telfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that \add is\add*, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, \add to\add* the telfth \add month\add*, that \add is\add*, the month Adar.

And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their las \add are\add* diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s las: therefore it \add is\add* not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

If it please the king, let it be ritten that they may be destroyed: and I ill pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring \add it\add* into the king’s treasuries.
And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jes’ enemy.
And the king said unto Haman, The silver \add is\add* given to thee, the people also, to do ith them as it seemeth good to thee.

Then ere the king’s scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there as ritten according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors that \add ere\add* over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the riting thereof, and \add to\add* every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus as it ritten, and sealed ith the king’s ring.

And the letters ere sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jes, both young and old, little children and omen, in one day, \add even\add* upon the thirteenth \add day\add* of the telfth month, hich \add is\add* the month Adar, and \add to take\add* the spoil of them for a prey.
The copy of the riting for a commandment to be given in every province \add as\add* published unto all people, that \add they\add* should be ready against that day.
The posts ent out, being hastened by the king’s commandment, and the decree as given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat don to drink; but the city Shushan as perplexed.
When Mordecai perceived all that as done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth ith ashes, and ent out into the midst of the city, and cried \add ith\add* a loud and a bitter cry;
and came even before the king’s gate: for none might enter into the king’s gate clothed ith sackcloth.

And in every province, hithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, \add there as\add* great mourning among the Jes, and fasting, and eeping, and ailing; \add and\add* many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

So Esther’s maids and her chamberlains came and told \add it\add* her. Then as the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take aay his sackcloth from him: but he received \add it\add* not.

Then called Esther for Hatach, \add one\add* of the king’s chamberlains, hom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to kno hat it \add as\add*, and hy it \add as\add*.
So Hatach ent forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, hich \add as\add* before the king’s gate.
And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the Jes, to destroy them.

Also he gave him the copy of the riting of the decree that as given at Shushan to destroy them, to she \add it\add* unto Esther, and to declare \add it\add* unto her, and to charge her that \add she\add* should go in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him for her people.
And Hatach came and told Esther the ords of Mordecai.
Again Esther spake unto Hatach, and gave him commandment unto Mordecai:

All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, do kno, that hosoever, \add hether\add* man or oman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, ho is not called, \add there is\add* one la of his to put \add him\add* to death, except such to hom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
And they told to Mordecai Esther’s ords.
Then Mordecai commanded to anser Esther, Think not ith thyself that \add thou\add* shalt escape \add in\add* the king’s house, more than all the Jes.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, \add then\add* shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jes from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and ho knoeth hether thou art come to the kingdom for \add such\add* a time as this?
Then Esther bade \add them\add* return Mordecai \add this anser\add*:

Go, gather together all the Jes that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day; I also and my maidens ill fast likeise; and so ill I go in unto the king, hich \add is\add* not according to the la: and if I perish, I perish.
So Mordecai ent his ay, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

No it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on \add her\add* royal \add apparel\add*, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

And it as \add so\add*, hen the king sa Esther the queen standing in the court, \add that\add* she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that \add as\add* in his hand. So Esther dre near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
Then said the king unto her, What ilt thou, queen Esther? and hat \add is\add* thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom.
And Esther ansered, If \add it seem\add* good unto the king, let the king and Haman come \add this\add* day unto the banquet that I have prepared for him.
Then the king said, Cause Haman to make haste, that \add he\add* may do as Esther hath said. So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

And the king said unto Esther at the banquet of ine, What \add is\add* thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: and hat \add is\add* thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.
Then ansered Esther, and said, My petition and my request \add is;\add*

if I have found favour in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition, and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I ill do to morro as the king hath said.
Then ent Haman forth that day joyful and ith a glad heart: but hen Haman sa Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he stood not up, nor moved for him, he as full \add of\add* indignation against Mordecai.
Nevertheless Haman refrained himself: and hen he came home, he sent and called for his friends, and Zeresh his ife.

And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all \add the things\add* here\add in\add* the king had promoted him, and ho he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.

Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no \add man\add* come in ith the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to morro \add am\add* I invited unto her also ith the king.
Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Je sitting at the king’s gate.

Then said Zeresh his ife and all his friends unto him, Let a gallos be made of fifty cubits high, and to morro speak thou unto the king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily ith the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he caused the gallos to be made.
On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they ere read before the king.
And it as found ritten, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, to of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door, ho sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.
And the king said, Who \add is\add* in the court? No Haman as come into the outard court of the king’s house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallos that he had prepared for him.
And the king’s servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

So Haman came in. And the king said unto him, What shall be done unto the man hom the king delighteth to honour? No Haman thought in his heart, To hom ould the king delight to do honour more than to myself?
And Haman ansered the king, \add For\add* the man hom the king delighteth to honour,
let the royal apparel be brought hich the king \add useth\add* to ear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and the cron royal hich is set upon his head:

and let \add this\add* apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man \add ithal\add* hom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man hom the king delighteth to honour.

Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, \add and\add* take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do \add even\add* so to Mordecai the Je, that sitteth at the king’s gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.

Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man hom the king delighteth to honour.
And Mordecai came again to the king’s gate. But Haman hasted to his house mourning, and having his head covered.

And Haman told Zeresh his ife and all his friends every \add thing\add* that had befallen him. Then said his ise \add men\add* and Zeresh his ife unto him, If Mordecai \add be\add* of the seed of the Jes, before hom thou hast begun to fall, thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt surely fall before him.
And hile they \add ere\add* yet talking ith him, came the king’s chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.
So the king and Haman came to banquet ith Esther the queen.

And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of ine, What \add is\add* thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and hat \add is\add* thy request? and it shall be performed, \add even\add* to the half of the kingdom.
Then Esther the queen ansered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:

for e are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if e had been sold for bondmen and bondomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king’s damage.
Then the king Ahasuerus ansered and said unto Esther the queen, Who \add is\add* he, and here \add is\add* he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
And Esther said, The adversary and enemy \add is\add* this icked Haman. Then Haman as afraid before the king and the queen.

And the king arising from the banquet of ine in his rath \add ent\add* into the palace garden: and Haman stood \add up\add* to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he sa that there as evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of ine; and Haman as fallen upon the bed hereon Esther \add as\add*. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the ord ent out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallos fifty cubits high, hich Haman had made for Mordecai, ho had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
So they hanged Haman on the gallos that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then as the king’s rath pacified.
On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jes’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told hat he \add as\add* unto her.
And the king took off his ring, hich he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell don at his feet, and besought him ith tears to put aay the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jes.
Then the king held out the golden sceptre toard Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,

and said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I \add be\add* pleasing in his eyes, let it be ritten to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, hich he rote to destroy the Jes hich \add are\add* in all the king’s provinces:
for ho can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or ho can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?

Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Je, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallos, because he laid his hand upon the Jes.

Write ye also for the Jes, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal \add it\add* ith the king’s ring: for the riting hich \add is\add* ritten in the king’s name, and sealed ith the king’s ring, may no man reverse.

A time to be born, and a time to die; A time to plant, and a time to pluck up \add that hich is\add* planted;
A time to kill, and a time to heal; A time to break don, and a time to build \add up;\add*
A time to eep, and a time to laugh; A time to mourn, and a time to dance;
A time to cast aay stones, and a time to gather stones together; A time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
A time to get, and a time to lose; A time to keep, and a time to cast aay;
A time to rent, and a time to se; A time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
A time to love, and a time to hate; A time of ar, and a time of peace.
What profit \add hath\add* he that orketh in \add that\add* here\add in\add* he laboureth?
I have seen the travail, hich God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
He hath made every \add thing\add* beautiful in his time: also he hath set the orld in their heart, so that no man can find out the ork that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
I kno that \add there is\add* no good in them, but for \add a man\add* to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it \add is\add* the gift of God.
I kno that, hatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth \add it\add*, that \add men\add* should fear before him.
That hich hath been, \add is\add* no; and \add that\add* hich \add is\add* to be hath already been; and God requireth that hich is past.
And moreover I sa under the sun the place of judgment, \add that\add* ickedness \add as\add* there; and the place of righteousness, \add that\add* iniquity \add as\add* there.
I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the icked: for \add there is\add* a time there for every purpose and for every ork.
I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that \add they\add* might see that they themselves are beasts.

For that hich befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all \add is\add* vanity.
All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Who knoeth the spirit of man that goeth upard, and the spirit of the beast that goeth donard to the earth?
Wherefore I perceive that \add there is\add* nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his on orks; for that \add is\add* his portion: for ho shall bring him to see hat shall be after him?

So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that \add are\add* done under the sun: and behold, the tears of such as ere oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors \add there as\add* poer; but they had no comforter.
Wherefore I praised the dead hich are already dead more than the living hich are yet alive.
Yea, better \add is he\add* than both they, hich hath not yet been, ho hath not seen the evil ork that is done under the sun.
Again, I considered all travail, and every right ork, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This \add is\add* also vanity and vexation of spirit.
The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his on flesh.
Better \add is\add* a handful \add ith\add* quietness, than both the hands full \add ith\add* travail and vexation of spirit.
Then I returned, and I sa vanity under the sun.

There is one \add alone\add*, and \add there is\add* not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet \add is there\add* no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied \add ith\add* riches; neither \add saith he\add*, For hom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This \add is\add* also vanity, yea, it \add is\add* a sore travail.
To \add are\add* better than one; because they have a good reard for their labour.
For if they fall, the one ill lift up his fello: but oe to him \add that is\add* alone hen he falleth; for \add he hath\add* not another to help him up.
Again, if to lie together, then they have heat: but ho can one be arm \add alone?\add*
And if one prevail against him, to shall ithstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Better \add is\add* a poor and a ise child than an old and foolish king, ho ill no more be admonished.
For out of prison he cometh to reign; hereas also \add he that is\add* born in his kingdom becometh poor.
I considered all the living hich alk under the sun, ith the second child that shall stand \add up\add* in his stead.

\add There is\add* no end of all the people, \add even\add* of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also \add is\add* vanity and vexation of spirit.
Keep thy foot hen thou goest to the house of God, and \add be\add* more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that \add they\add* do evil.
Be not rash ith thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter \add any\add* thing before God: for God \add is\add* in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy ords be fe.
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice \add is knon\add* by multitude of ords.
When thou voest a vo unto God, defer not to pay it; for \add he hath\add* no pleasure in fools: pay that hich thou hast voed.
Better \add is it\add* that thou shouldest not vo, than that thou shouldest vo and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it \add as\add* an error: herefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the ork of thine hands?
For in the multitude of dreams and many ords \add there are\add* also \add divers\add* vanities: but fear thou God.

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for \add he that is\add* higher than the highest regardeth; and \add there be\add* higher than they.
Moreover the profit of the earth \add is\add* for all: the king \add himself\add* is served by the field.
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied \add ith\add* silver; nor he that loveth abundance \add ith\add* increase: this \add is\add* also vanity.
When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and hat good \add is there\add* to the oners thereof, saving the beholding \add of them\add* ith their eyes?
The sleep of a labouring \add man is\add* seet, hether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich ill not suffer him to sleep.
There is a sore evil \add hich\add* I have seen under the sun, \add namely\add*, riches kept for the oners thereof to their hurt.
But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and \add there is\add* nothing in his hand.
As he came forth of his mother’s omb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, hich he may carry aay in his hand.
And this also \add is\add* a sore evil, \add that\add* in all points as he came, so shall he go: and hat profit hath he that hath laboured for the ind?
All his days also he eateth in darkness, and \add he hath\add* much sorro and rath ith his sickness.

Behold \add that\add* hich I have seen: \add it is\add* good and comely \add for one\add* to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, hich God giveth him: for it \add is\add* his portion.
Every man also to hom God hath given riches and ealth, and hath given him poer to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this \add is\add* the gift of God.
For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God ansereth \add him\add* in the joy of his heart.
There is an evil hich I have seen under the sun, and it \add is\add* common among men:

a man to hom God hath given riches, ealth, and honour, so that he anteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not poer to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this \add is\add* vanity, and it \add is\add* an evil disease.

If a man beget an hundred \add children\add*, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled ith good, and also \add that\add* he have no burial; I say, \add that\add* an untimely birth \add is\add* better than he.
For he cometh in ith vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered ith darkness.
Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor knon \add any thing:\add* this hath more rest than the other.
Yea, though he live a thousand years tice \add told\add*, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
All the labour of man \add is\add* for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
For hat hath the ise more than the fool? hat hath the poor, that knoeth to alk before the living?
Better \add is\add* the sight of the eyes than the andering of the desire: this \add is\add* also vanity and vexation of spirit.
That hich hath been is named already, and \add it is\add* knon that it \add is\add* man: neither may he contend ith him that \add is\add* mightier than he.
Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, hat \add is\add* man the better?
For ho knoeth hat \add is\add* good for man in \add this\add* life, all the days of his vain life hich he spendeth as a shado? for ho can tell a man hat shall be after him under the sun?
A \add good\add* name \add is\add* better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
\add It is\add* better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that \add is\add* the end of all men; and the living ill lay \add it\add* to his heart.
Sorro \add is\add* better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
The heart of the ise \add is\add* in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools \add is\add* in the house of mirth.
\add It is\add* better to hear the rebuke of the ise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so \add is\add* the laughter of the fool: this also \add is\add* vanity.
Surely oppression maketh a ise \add man\add* mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
Better \add is\add* the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: \add and\add* the patient in spirit \add is\add* better than the proud in spirit.
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
Say not thou, What is \add the cause\add* that the former days ere better than these? for thou dost not inquire isely concerning this.
Wisdom \add is\add* good ith an inheritance: and \add by it there is\add* profit to them that see the sun.
For isdom \add is\add* a defence, \add and\add* money \add is\add* a defence: but the excellency of knoledge \add is, that\add* isdom giveth life to them that have it.
Consider the ork of God: for ho can make \add that\add* straight, hich he hath made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

All \add things\add* have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just \add man\add* that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a icked \add man\add* that prolongeth \add his life\add* in his ickedness.
Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over ise: hy shouldest thou destroy thyself?
Be not over much icked, neither be thou foolish: hy shouldest thou die before thy time?
\add It is\add* good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this ithdra not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
Wisdom strengtheneth the ise more than ten mighty \add men\add* hich are in the city.
For \add there is\add* not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
Also take no heed unto all ords that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
for oftentimes also thine on heart knoeth that thou thyself likeise hast cursed others.
All this have I proved by isdom: I said, I ill be ise; but it \add as\add* far from me.
That hich is far off, and exceeding deep, ho can find it out?
I applied mine heart to kno, and to search, and to seek out isdom, and the reason \add of things\add*, and to kno the ickedness of folly, even of foolishness \add and\add* madness:

and I find more bitter than death the oman, hose heart \add is\add* snares and nets, \add and\add* her hands \add as\add* bands: hoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
Behold, this have I found, saith the Preacher, \add counting\add* one by one, to find out the account:
hich yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a oman among all those have I not found.
Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
Who \add is\add* as the ise \add man?\add* and ho knoeth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s isdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
I \add counsel thee\add* to keep the king’s commandment, and \add that\add* in regard of the oath of God.
Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth hatsoever pleaseth him.
Where the ord of a king \add is, there is\add* poer: and ho may say unto him, What doest thou?
Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a ise \add man’s\add* heart discerneth \add both\add* time and judgment.
Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man \add is\add* great upon him.
For he knoeth not that hich shall be: for ho can tell him hen it shall be?

\add There is\add* no man that hath poer over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither \add hath he\add* poer in the day of death: and \add there is\add* no discharge in \add that\add* ar; neither shall ickedness deliver those that are given to it.
All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every ork that is done under the sun: \add there is\add* a time herein one man ruleth over another to his on hurt.
And so I sa the icked buried, ho had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they ere forgotten in the city here they had so done: this \add is\add* also vanity.
Because sentence \add against\add* an evil ork is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Though a sinner do evil an hundred \add times\add*, and his \add days\add* be prolonged, yet surely I kno that it shall be ell ith them that fear God, hich fear before him:
but it shall not be ell ith the icked, neither shall he prolong \add his\add* days, \add hich are\add* as a shado; because he feareth not before God.

There is a vanity hich is done upon the earth; that there be just \add men\add*, unto hom it happeneth according to the ork of the icked; again, there be icked \add men\add*, to hom it happeneth according to the ork of the righteous: I said that this also \add is\add* vanity.

Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better \add thing\add* under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide ith him of his labour the days of his life, hich God giveth him under the sun.
When I applied mine heart to kno isdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also \add there is that\add* neither day nor night seeth sleep ith his eyes:)

then I beheld all the ork of God, that a man cannot find out the ork that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek \add it\add* out, yet he shall not find \add it;\add* yea further, though a ise \add man\add* think to kno \add it\add*, yet shall he not be able to find \add it\add*.

For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the ise, and their orks, \add are\add* in the hand of God: no man knoeth either love or hatred \add by\add* all \add that is\add* before them.

All \add things come\add* alike to all: \add there is\add* one event to the righteous, and to the icked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as \add is\add* the good, so \add is\add* the sinner; \add and\add* he that seareth, as he that feareth an oath.

This \add is\add* an evil among all \add things\add* that are done under the sun, that \add there is\add* one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full \add of\add* evil, and madness \add is\add* in their heart hile they live, and after that \add they go\add* to the dead.
For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog \add is\add* better than a dead lion.
For the living kno that they shall die: but the dead kno not any thing, neither have they any more a reard; for the memory of them is forgotten.
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is no perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any \add thing\add* that is done under the sun.
Go \add thy ay,\add* eat thy bread ith joy, and drink thy ine ith a merry heart; for God no accepteth thy orks.
Let thy garments be alays hite; and let thy head lack no ointment.

Live joyfully ith the ife hom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, hich he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that \add is\add* thy portion in \add this\add* life, and in thy labour hich thou takest under the sun.
Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do \add it\add* ith thy might; for \add there is\add* no ork, nor device, nor knoledge, nor isdom, in the grave, hither thou goest.

I returned, and sa under the sun, that the race \add is\add* not to the sift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the ise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

For man also knoeth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so \add are\add* the sons of men snared in an evil time, hen it falleth suddenly upon them.
This isdom have I seen also under the sun, and it \add seemed\add* great unto me:
\add there as\add* a little city, and fe men ithin it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bularks against it:
no there as found in it a poor ise man, and he by his isdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that \add same\add* poor man.
Then said I, Wisdom \add is\add* better than strength: nevertheless the poor \add man’s\add* isdom \add is\add* despised, and his ords \add are\add* not heard.
The ords of ise \add men are\add* heard in quiet, more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
Wisdom \add is\add* better than eapons of ar: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: \add so doth\add* a little folly \add him that is\add* in reputation for isdom \add and\add* honour.
A ise \add man’s\add* heart \add is\add* at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
Yea also, hen he that is a fool alketh by the ay, his isdom faileth \add him\add*, and he saith to every one \add that\add* he \add is\add* a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
There is an evil \add hich\add* I have seen under the sun, as an error \add hich\add* proceedeth from the ruler:
folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in lo place.
I have seen servants upon horses, and princes alking as servants upon the earth.
He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and hoso breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt thereith; \add and\add* he that cleaveth ood shall be endangered thereby.
If the iron be blunt, and he do not het the edge, then must he put to more strength: but isdom \add is\add* profitable to direct.
Surely the serpent ill bite ithout enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
The ords of a ise \add man’s\add* mouth \add are\add* gracious; but the lips of a fool ill sallo up himself.
The beginning of the ords of his mouth \add is\add* foolishness: and the end of his talk \add is\add* mischievous madness.
A fool also is full of ords: a man cannot tell hat shall be; and hat shall be after him, ho can tell him?
The labour of the foolish earieth every one of them, because he knoeth not ho to go to the city.
Woe to thee, O land, hen thy king \add is\add* a child, and thy princes eat in the morning.
Blessed \add art\add* thou, O land, hen thy king \add is\add* the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness.
By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
A feast is made for laughter, and ine maketh merry: but money ansereth all \add things\add*.
Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that hich hath ings shall tell the matter.
Cast thy bread upon the aters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knoest not hat evil shall be upon the earth.

If the clouds be full \add of\add* rain, they empty \add themselves\add* upon the earth: and if the tree fall toard the south, or toard the north, \add in\add* the place here the tree falleth, there it shall be.
He that observeth the ind shall not so; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
As thou knoest not hat \add is\add* the ay of the spirit, \add nor\add* ho the bones \add do gro\add* in the omb of her that is ith child: even so thou knoest not the orks of God ho maketh all.
In the morning so thy seed, and in the evening ithhold not thine hand: for thou knoest not hether shall prosper, either this or that, or hether they both \add shall be\add* alike good.
Truly the light \add is\add* seet, and a pleasant \add thing it is\add* for the eyes to behold the sun:
but if a man live many years, \add and\add* rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh \add is\add* vanity.

Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and alk in the ays of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but kno thou, that for all these \add things\add* God ill bring thee into judgment.
Therefore remove sorro from thy heart, and put aay evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth \add are\add* vanity.
Remember no thy Creator in the days of thy youth, hile the evil days come not, nor the years dra nigh, hen thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
hile the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
in the day hen the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bo themselves, and the grinders cease because they are fe, and those that look out of the indos be darkened,
and the doors shall be shut in the streets, hen the sound of the grinding is lo, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought lo;

also \add hen\add* they shall be afraid of \add that hich is\add* high, and fears \add shall be\add* in the ay, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bol be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the heel broken at the cistern.
Then shall the dust return to the earth as it as: and the spirit shall return unto God ho gave it.
Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all \add is\add* vanity.
And moreover, because the Preacher as ise, he still taught the people knoledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, \add and\add* set in order many proverbs.
The Preacher sought to find out acceptable ords: and \add that hich as\add* ritten \add as\add* upright, \add even\add* ords of truth.
The ords of the ise \add are\add* as goads, and as nails fastened \add by\add* the masters of assemblies, \add hich\add* are given from one shepherd.
And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books \add there is\add* no end; and much study \add is\add* a eariness of the flesh.
Let us hear the conclusion of the hole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this \add is\add* the hole \add duty of\add* man.
For God shall bring every ork into judgment, ith every secret \add thing\add*, hether \add it be\add* good, or hether \add it be\add* evil.
\sc The\sc* song of songs, hich \add is\add* Solomon’s.
Let him kiss me ith the kisses of his mouth: For thy love \add is\add* better than ine.
Because of the savour of thy good ointments Thy name \add is as\add* ointment poured forth, Therefore do the virgins love thee.
Dra me, e ill run after thee: The king hath brought me \add into\add* his chambers: We ill be glad and rejoice in thee, We ill remember thy love more than ine: The upright love thee.
I \add am\add* black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

Look not upon me, because I \add am\add* black, Because the sun hath looked upon me: My mother’s children ere angry ith me; They made me the keeper of the vineyards; \add But\add* mine on vineyard have I not kept.
Tell me, O thou hom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest, here thou makest \add thy flock\add* to rest at noon: For hy should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions? \b
If thou kno not, O thou fairest among omen, Go thy ay forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
I have compared thee, O my love, To a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Thy cheeks are comely ith ros \add of jeels\add*, Thy neck ith chains \add of gold\add*.
We ill make thee borders of gold With studs of silver. \b
While the king \add sitteth\add* at his table, My spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
A bundle of myrrh \add is\add* my ell-beloved unto me; He shall lie all night betixt my breasts.
My beloved \add is\add* unto me \add as\add* a cluster of camphire In the vineyards of En-gedi.
Behold, thou \add art\add* fair, my love; behold, thou \add art\add* fair; Thou \add hast\add* doves’ eyes. \b
Behold, thou \add art\add* fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our bed \add is\add* green.
The beams of our house \add are\add* cedar, \add And\add* our rafters of fir. \b
I am the rose of Sharon, \add And\add* the lily of the valleys. \b
As the lily among thorns, So \add is\add* my love among the daughters. \b
As the apple tree among the trees of the ood, So \add is\add* my beloved among the sons. I sat don under his shado ith great delight, And his fruit \add as\add* seet to my taste.
He brought me to the banqueting house, And his banner over me \add as\add* love.
Stay me ith flagons, comfort me ith apples: For I \add am\add* sick of love.
His left hand \add is\add* under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.
I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, and by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor aake \add my\add* love, till he please. \b
The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh Leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
My beloved \add is\add* like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our all, He looketh forth at the indos, Sheing himself through the lattice.
My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come aay.
