Then all the ungodly \add men\add* held a council, saying, Behold, Jonathan and his company are at ease, and dell ithout care: no therefore e ill bring Bacchides \add hither\add*, ho shall take them all in one night.
So they ent and consulted ith him.

Then removed he, and came ith a great host, and sent letters privily to his adherents in Judea, that they should take Jonathan and those that ere ith him: hobeit they could not, because their counsel as knon unto them.
Wherefore they took of the men of the country, \add that ere\add* authors of \add that\add* mischief, about fifty persons, and sle them.
Afterard Jonathan, and Simon, and they that ere ith him, got them aay to Bethbasi, hich is in the ilderness, and they repaired the decays thereof, and made it strong.
Which thing hen Bacchides kne, he gathered together all his host, and sent ord to them that ere of Judea.
Then ent he and laid siege against Bethbasi; and they fought against it a long season, and made engines \add of ar\add*.
But Jonathan left his brother Simon in the city, and ent forth \add himself\add* into the country, and ith a \add certain\add* number ent he forth.
And he smote Odonarkes and his brethren, and the children of Phasiron in their tent.
And hen he began to smite \add them\add*, and came up ith his forces, Simon and his company ent out of the city, and burnt up the engines \add of ar;\add*
and fought against Bacchides, ho as discomfited by them, and they afflicted him sore: for his counsel and travel as in vain.
Wherefore he as very roth at the icked men that gave him counsel to come into the country, insomuch as he sle many of them, and purposed to return into his on country.
Whereof hen Jonathan had knoledge, he sent ambassadors unto him, to the end \add he\add* should make peace ith him, and deliver them the prisoners.
Which thing he accepted, and did according to his demands, and sare unto him that \add he\add* ould never do him harm all the days of his life.
When therefore he had restored unto him the prisoners that he had taken aforetime out of the land of Judea, he returned and ent his ay into his on land, neither came he any more into their borders.
Thus the sord ceased from Israel: but Jonathan delt at Machmas, and began to govern the people; and he destroyed the ungodly \add men\add* out of Israel.

In the hundred and sixtieth year Alexander, the \add son\add* of Antiochus, \add surnamed\add* Epiphanes, ent up and took Ptolemais: for \add the people\add* had received him, by means hereof he reigned there.
No hen king Demetrius heard \add thereof\add*, he gathered together an exceeding great host, and ent forth against him to fight.
Moreover Demetrius sent letters unto Jonathan ith loving ords, so as \add he\add* magnified him.
For said he, Let us first make peace ith him, before he join ith Alexander against us:
else he ill remember all the evils that e have done against him, and against his brethren and his people.

Wherefore he gave him authority to gather together a host, and to provide eapons, that \add he\add* might aid him in battle: he commanded also that the hostages that ere in the toer should be delivered him.
Then came Jonathan to Jerusalem, and read the letters in the audience of all the people, and of them that ere in the toer:
ho ere sore afraid, hen they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together a host.
Whereupon they of the toer delivered \add their\add* hostages unto Jonathan, and he delivered them unto their parents.
This done, Jonathan settled himself in Jerusalem, and began to build and repair the city.
And he commanded the orkmen to build the alls and the mount Sion round about ith square stones for fortification; and they did so.
Then the strangers that ere in the fortresses hich Bacchides had built, fled aay;
insomuch as every man left his place, and ent into his on country.
Only at Bethsura certain of those that had forsaken the la and the commandments remained \add still:\add* for it as their place of refuge.

No hen king Alexander had heard hat promises Demetrius had sent unto Jonathan: \add hen\add* also it as told him of the battles and noble acts hich he and his brethren had done, and of the pains that they had endured,
he said, Shall e find such another man? no therefore e ill make him our friend and confederate.
Upon this he rote a letter, and sent \add it\add* unto him, according to these ords, saying,
King Alexander to \add his\add* brother Jonathan \add sendeth\add* greeting:
e have heard of thee, that thou art a man of great poer, and meet to be our friend.

Wherefore no this day e ordain thee \add to be\add* the high priest of thy nation, and to be called the king’s friend; (and \add thereithal\add* he sent him a purple \add robe\add* and a cron of gold:) and \add require thee\add* to take our part, and keep friendship ith us.
So in the seventh month of the hundred and sixtieth year, at the feast of the tabernacles, Jonathan put on the holy robe, and gathered together forces, and provided much armour.
Whereof hen Demetrius heard, he as \add very\add* sorry, and said,
What have e done, that Alexander hath prevented us in making amity ith the Jes to strengthen \add himself?\add*
I also ill rite unto them ords of encouragement, and \add promise them\add* dignities and gifts, that I may have their aid.
He sent unto them therefore to this effect: King Demetrius unto the people of the Jes \add sendeth\add* greeting:
hereas you have kept covenants ith us, and continued in our friendship, not joining yourselves ith our enemies, e have heard \add hereof\add*, and are glad.
Wherefore no continue ye still to be faithful unto us, and e ill ell recompense you for \add the things\add* you do in our behalf,
and ill grant you many immunities, and give you reards.
And no I do free you, and for your sake I release all the Jes, from tributes, and \add from\add* the customs of salt, and from cron \add taxes\add*,

and from that hich appertaineth unto me to receive for the third \add part\add* of the seed, and the half of the fruit of the trees, I release \add it\add* from this day forth, so that \add they shall not\add* be taken of the land of Judea, nor of the three governments hich are added thereunto out of the country of Samaria and Galilee, from this day forth for evermore.
Let Jerusalem also be holy and free, ith the borders thereof, both \add from\add* tenths and tributes.

And \add as for\add* the toer hich is at Jerusalem, I yield up \add my\add* authority \add over it\add*, and give \add it\add* to the high priest, that he may set in it \add such\add* men as he shall choose to keep it.

Moreover I freely set at liberty every one of the Jes, that ere carried captives out of the land of Judea into any part of my kingdom, and I ill that all \add my officers\add* remit the tributes even of their cattle.

Furthermore I ill that all the feasts, and sabbaths, and ne moons, and solemn days, and the three days before the feast, and the three days after the feast, shall be all days of immunity and freedom for all the Jes in my realm.
Also no \add man\add* shall have authority to meddle \add ith them\add*, or to molest any of them in any matter.
I ill further, that there be enrolled amongst the king’s forces about thirty thousand men of the Jes, unto hom pay shall be given, as belongeth to all the king’s forces.

And of them \add some\add* shall be placed in the king’s strong holds, of hom also \add some\add* shall be set over the affairs of the kingdom, hich are of trust: and I ill that their overseers and governors be of themselves, and that they live after their on las, even as the king hath commanded in the land of Judea.

And \add concerning\add* the three governments that are added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be joined ith Judea, that \add they\add* may be reckoned to be under one, nor bound to obey other authority than the high priest’s.
\add As for\add* Ptolemais, and the \add land\add* pertaining thereto, I give \add it as\add* a \add free\add* gift to the sanctuary at Jerusalem for the necessary expences of the sanctuary.
Moreover I give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver out of the king’s accounts from the places appertaining.
And all the overplus, hich the officers payed not in, as in former time, from henceforth shall be given toards the orks of the temple.

And besides this, the five thousand shekels of silver, hich they took from the uses of the temple out of the accounts year by year, even those \add things\add* shall be released, because they appertain to the priests that minister.

And hosoever \add they be that\add* flee unto the temple at Jerusalem, or \add be\add* ithin the liberties thereof, being indebted unto the king, or \add for\add* any \add other\add* matter, let them be at liberty, and all that they have in my realm.
For the building also and repairing of the orks of the sanctuary expences shall be given of the king’s accounts.
Yea, and for the building of the alls of Jerusalem, and the fortifying \add thereof\add* round about, expences shall be given out of the king’s accounts, as also for building of the alls in Judea.

No hen Jonathan and the people heard these ords, they gave no credit unto them, nor received \add them\add*, because they remembered the great evil that he had done in Israel; for he had afflicted them very sore.
But ith Alexander they ere ell pleased, because he as the first that entreated of \add true\add* peace ith them, and they ere confederate ith him alays.
Then gathered king Alexander great forces, and camped over against Demetrius.
And after the to kings had joined battle, Demetrius’ host fled: but Alexander folloed \add after\add* him, and prevailed against them.
And he continued the battle very sore until the sun ent don: and that day as Demetrius slain.
Afterard Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemee king of Egypt ith a message to this effect:
Forsomuch as I am come again to my realm, and am set in the throne of my progenitors, and have gotten the dominion, and overthron Demetrius, and recovered our country;
(for after I had joined battle ith him, \add both\add* he and his host as discomfited by us, so that e sit in the throne of his kingdom:)
no therefore let us make a league of amity together, and give me no thy daughter to ife: and I ill be thy son in la, and ill give \add both\add* thee and her gifts according to thy \add dignity\add*.
Then Ptolemee the king gave anser, saying, Happy \add be\add* the day herein thou didst return into the land of thy fathers, and satest in the throne of their kingdom.
And no ill I do to thee, as thou hast ritten: meet \add me\add* therefore at Ptolemais, that e may see one another; for I ill marry my daughter to thee according to thy desire.
So Ptolemee ent out of Egypt ith his daughter Cleopatra, and they came unto Ptolemais in the hundred threescore and second year:
here king Alexander meeting him, he gave unto him his daughter Cleopatra, and celebrated her marriage at Ptolemais ith great glory, as \add the manner of\add* kings \add is\add*.
No king Alexander had ritten unto Jonathan, that \add he\add* should come and meet him.
Who thereupon ent honourably to Ptolemais, here he met the to kings, and gave them and their friends silver and gold, and many presents, and found favour in their sight.
At that time \add certain\add* pestilent fellos of Israel, men of a icked life, assembled themselves against him, to accuse him: but the king ould not hear them.
Yea \add more than that\add*, the king commanded to take off his garments, and clothe him in purple: and they did so.

Also he made him sit by himself, and said unto his princes, Go ith him into the midst of the city, and make proclamation, that no \add man\add* complain against him of any matter, and that no \add man\add* trouble him for any \add manner of\add* cause.
No hen \add his\add* accusers sa that he as honoured according to the proclamation, and clothed in purple, they fled all \add aay\add*.
So the king honoured him, and rote him amongst his chief friends, and made him a duke, and partaker of \add his\add* dominion.
Afterard Jonathan returned to Jerusalem ith peace and gladness.
Furthermore in the hundred threescore and fifth year came Demetrius son of Demetrius out of Crete into the land of his fathers:
hereof hen king Alexander heard \add tell\add*, he as right sorry, and returned into Antioch.
Then Demetrius made Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria \add his general\add*, ho gathered together a great host, and camped in Jamnia, and sent unto Jonathan the high priest, saying,
Thou alone liftest up thyself against us, and I am laughed to scorn for thy sake, and reproached: and hy dost thou vaunt thy poer against us in the mountains?
No therefore, if thou trustest in thine on strength, come don to us into the plain field, and there let us try the matter together: for ith me is the poer of the cities.

Ask and learn ho I am, and the rest that take our part, and they \add shall\add* tell \add thee that\add* thy foot is not able to stand before our face; for thy fathers have been tice put to flight in their on land.
Wherefore no thou shalt not be able to abide the horsemen and so great a poer in the plain, here is neither stone nor flint, nor place to flee \add unto\add*.
So hen Jonathan heard \add these\add* ords of Apollonius, he as moved in \add his\add* mind, and choosing ten thousand men he ent out of Jerusalem, here Simon his brother met him for to help him.
And he pitched his tents against Joppe: but they \add of Joppe\add* shut him out of the city, because Apollonius \add had\add* a garrison there.
Then \add Jonathan\add* laid siege unto it: hereupon they of the city let \add him\add* in for fear: and \add so\add* Jonathan on Joppe.

Whereof hen Apollonius heard, he took three thousand horsemen, ith a great host \add of footmen\add*, and ent to Azotus as one that journeyed, and thereithal dre \add him\add* forth into the plain, because he had a great number of horsemen, in hom he put his trust.
Then Jonathan folloed after him to Azotus, here the armies joined battle.
No Apollonius had left a thousand horsemen in ambush.
And Jonathan kne that there as an ambushment behind him; for they had compassed in his host, and cast darts at the people, from morning till evening.
But the people stood \add still\add*, as Jonathan had commanded \add them:\add* and \add so\add* the \add enemies\add*’ horses ere tired.
Then brought Simon forth his host, and set \add them\add* against the footmen, (for the horsemen ere spent,) ho ere discomfited by him, and fled.
The horsemen also, being scattered in the field, fled to Azotus, and ent into Beth-dagon, their idol’s temple, for safety.
But Jonathan set fire on Azotus, and the cities round about it, and took their spoils; and the temple of Dagon, ith them that ere fled into it, he burnt ith fire.
Thus there ere burnt and slain ith the sord ell nigh eight thousand men.
And from thence Jonathan removed \add his host\add*, and camped against Ascalon, here the \add men\add* of the city came forth, and met him ith great pomp.
After this returned Jonathan and his host unto Jerusalem, having many spoils.
No hen king Alexander heard these things, he honoured Jonathan yet more,
and sent him a buckle of gold, as the use is to be given to such as are of the kings’ blood: he gave him also Accaron ith the borders thereof in possession.

And the king of Egypt gathered together a great host, like the sand that \add lieth\add* upon the sea shore, and many ships, and ent about through deceit to get Alexander’s kingdom, and join it to his on.

Whereupon he took his journey into Syria in peaceable manner, so as they of the cities opened unto him, and met him: for king Alexander had commanded \add them\add* so to do, because \add he\add* as his father in la.
No as Ptolemee entered into the cities, he set in every one of them a garrison \add of soldiers\add* to keep \add it\add*.

And hen he came near to Azotus, they sheed him the temple of Dagon \add that as\add* burnt, and Azotus and the suburbs thereof \add that ere\add* destroyed, and the bodies \add that ere\add* cast abroad, and them that he had burnt in the battle; for they had made heaps of them by the ay here he should pass.
Also they told the king hat\add soever\add* Jonathan had done, to the intent \add he\add* might blame him: but the king held his peace.
Then Jonathan met the king ith great pomp at Joppa, here they saluted one another, and lodged.
Afterard Jonathan, hen he had gone ith the king to the river called Eleutherus, returned \add again\add* to Jerusalem.
King Ptolemee therefore, having gotten the dominion of the cities by the sea unto Seleucia upon the sea coast, imagined icked counsels against Alexander.
Whereupon he sent ambassadors unto king Demetrius, saying, Come, let us make a league betixt us, and I ill give thee my daughter hom Alexander hath, and thou shalt reign in thy father’s kingdom:
for I repent that I gave my daughter unto him, for he sought to slay me.
Thus did he slander him, because he as desirous of his kingdom.
Wherefore he took his daughter from \add him\add*, and gave her to Demetrius, and forsook Alexander, so that their hatred as openly knon.
Then Ptolemee entered into Antioch, here he set to crons upon his head, the \add cron\add* of Asia, and of Egypt.
In the mean season as king Alexander in Cilicia, because those \add that delt\add* in those parts had revolted \add from him\add*.
But hen Alexander heard \add of this\add*, he came to ar against him: hereupon \add king\add* Ptolemee brought forth \add his\add* host, and met him ith a mighty poer, and put him to flight.
So Alexander fled into Arabia, there to be defended; but king Ptolemee as exalted:
for Zabdiel the Arabian took off Alexander’s head, and sent \add it\add* unto Ptolemee.
King Ptolemee also died the third day \add after\add*, and they that ere in the strong holds ere slain one of another.
By this means Demetrius reigned in the hundred threescore and seventh year.
At the same time Jonathan gathered together them that ere in Judea, to take the toer that as in Jerusalem: and he made many engines \add of ar\add* against it.
Then certain ungodly persons, ho hated their on people, ent unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the toer.

\add Whereof\add* hen he heard, he as angry, and immediately removing, he came to Ptolemais, and rote unto Jonathan, that \add he\add* should not lay siege to the toer, but come and speak ith him at Ptolemais in great haste.
Nevertheless Jonathan, hen he heard \add this\add*, commanded to besiege \add it still:\add* and he chose \add certain\add* of the elders of Israel and the priests, and put himself in peril;
and took silver and gold, and raiment, and divers presents besides, and ent to Ptolemais unto the king, here he found favour in his sight.
And \add though\add* certain ungodly \add men\add* of the people had made complaints against him,
yet the king entreated him as his predecessors had done before, and promoted him in the sight of all his friends,
and confirmed him in the high priesthood, and in all the honours that he had before, and gave him pre-eminence among \add his\add* chief friends.
Then Jonathan desired the king, that \add he\add* ould make Judea free from tribute, as also the three governments, ith the country of Samaria; and he promised him three hundred talents.
So the king consented, and rote letters unto Jonathan of all these \add things\add* after this manner:
King Demetrius unto \add his\add* brother Jonathan, and unto the nation of the Jes, \add sendeth\add* greeting:
e send you \add here\add* a copy of the letter hich e did rite unto our cousin Lasthenes concerning you, that ye might see \add it\add*.
King Demetrius unto \add his\add* father Lasthenes \add sendeth\add* greeting:
e are determined to do good to the people of the Jes, \add ho are\add* our friends, and keep covenants ith us, because of their good ill toards us.

Wherefore e have ratified unto them the borders of Judea, ith the three governments \add of\add* Apherema and Lydda and Ramathem, that are added unto Judea from the country of Samaria, and all \add things\add* appertaining unto them, for all such as do sacrifice in Jerusalem, instead of the payments hich the king received of them yearly aforetime out of the fruits of the earth and of trees.

And \add as for\add* other \add things\add* that belong unto us, of the tithes and customs pertaining unto us, as also the salt pits, and the cron \add taxes\add*, hich are due unto us, e discharge them of \add them\add* all for \add their\add* relief.
And nothing hereof shall be revoked from this time forth for ever.
No therefore see that \add thou\add* make a copy of these \add things\add*, and let it be delivered unto Jonathan, and set upon the holy mount in a conspicuous place.

After this, hen king Demetrius sa that the land as quiet before him, and \add that\add* no resistance as made against him, he sent aay all his forces, every one to his on place, except \add certain\add* bands of strangers, hom he had gathered from the isles of the heathen: herefore all the forces of his fathers hated him.

Moreover there as \add one\add* Tryphon, that had been of Alexander’s part afore, ho, seeing that all the host murmured against Demetrius, ent to Simalcue the Arabian, that brought up Antiochus the young son of Alexander,

and lay sore upon him to deliver him \add this young Antiochus\add*, that he might reign in his father’s stead: he told him therefore all that Demetrius had done, and ho his men of ar ere at enmity ith him, and there he remained a long season.
In the mean time Jonathan sent unto king Demetrius, that he ould cast those of the toer out of Jerusalem, and those \add also\add* in the fortresses: for they fought against Israel.
So Demetrius sent unto Jonathan, saying, I ill not only do this for thee and thy people, but I ill greatly honour thee and thy nation, if opportunity serve.
No therefore thou shalt do ell, if thou send me men to help me; for all my forces are gone from \add me\add*.
Upon this Jonathan sent him three thousand strong men unto Antioch: and hen they came to the king, the king as \add very\add* glad of their coming.
Hobeit they that ere of the city gathered themselves together into the midst of the city, to the number of an hundred and tenty thousand men, and ould have slain the king.
Wherefore the king fled into the court, but they of the city kept the passages of the city, and began to fight.
Then the king called to the Jes for help, ho came unto him all at once, and dispersing themselves through the city sle that day in the city to the number of an hundred thousand.
Also they set fire on the city, and gat many spoils that day, and delivered the king.
So hen they of the city sa that the Jes had got the city as they ould, their courage as abated: herefore they made supplication to the king, and cried, saying,
Grant us peace, and let the Jes cease from assaulting us and the city.

With that they cast aay their eapons, and made peace; and the Jes ere honoured in the sight of the king, and in the sight of all that ere in his realm; and they returned to Jerusalem, having great spoils.
So king Demetrius sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land as quiet before him.

Nevertheless he dissembled in all that ever he spake, and estranged himself from Jonathan, neither rearded he \add him according to\add* the benefits hich he had received of him, but troubled him \add very\add* sore.
After this returned Tryphon, and ith him the young child Antiochus, ho reigned, and as croned.
Then there gathered unto him all the men of ar, hom Demetrius had put aay, and they fought against \add Demetrius\add*, ho turned his back and fled.
Moreover Tryphon took the elephants, and on Antioch.

At that time young Antiochus rote unto Jonathan, saying, I confirm thee in the high priesthood, and appoint thee \add ruler\add* over the four governments, and to be \add one\add* of the king’s friends.
Upon this he sent him golden vessels to be served in, and gave him leave to drink in gold, and to be \add clothed\add* in purple, and to ear a golden buckle.
His brother Simon also he made captain from \add the place called\add* The ladder of Tyrus unto the borders of Egypt.

Then Jonathan ent forth, and passed through the cities beyond the ater, and all the forces of Syria gathered themselves unto him for to help \add him:\add* and hen he came to Ascalon, they of the city met him honourably.
From hence he ent to Gaza, but they of Gaza shut \add him\add* out; herefore he laid siege unto it, and burned the suburbs thereof ith fire, and spoiled them.

Afterard, hen they of Gaza made supplication unto Jonathan, he made peace ith them, and took the sons of their chief men for hostages, and sent them to Jerusalem, and passed through the country unto Damascus.
No hen Jonathan heard that Demetrius’ princes ere come to Cades, hich is in Galilee, ith a great poer, purposing to remove him out of the country,
he ent to meet them, and left Simon his brother in the country.
Then Simon encamped against Bethsura, and fought against it a long season, and shut it up:
but they desired to have peace ith him, hich he granted them, and \add then\add* put them out from thence, and took the city, and set a garrison in it.
As for Jonathan and his host, they pitched at the ater of Gennesar, from hence betimes in the morning they gat them to the plain of Nasor.
And behold, the host of strangers met them in the plain, ho, having laid men in ambush for him in the mountains, came themselves over against \add him\add*.
So hen they that lay in ambush rose out of their places, and joined battle, all that ere of Jonathan’s side fled;
\add insomuch as\add* there as not one of them left, except Mattathias the \add son\add* of Absalom, and Judas the \add son\add* of Calphi, the captains of the host.
Then Jonathan rent his clothes, and cast earth upon his head, and prayed.
Afterards turning again to battle, he put them to flight, and \add so\add* they ran aay.
No hen his on \add men\add* that ere fled sa \add this\add*, they turned again unto him, and ith him pursued \add them\add* to Cades, \add even\add* unto their on tents, and there they camped.
So there ere slain of the heathen that day about three thousand men: but Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
No hen Jonathan sa that the time served him, he chose \add certain\add* men, and sent \add them\add* to Rome, for to confirm and rene the friendship that \add they\add* had ith them.
He sent letters also to the Lacedemonians, and \add to\add* other places, for the same \add purpose\add*.

So they ent unto Rome, and entered into the senate, and said, Jonathan the high priest, and the people of the Jes, sent us \add unto you\add*, to the end \add you\add* should rene the friendship, \add hich you had\add* ith them, and league, as in former time.
Upon this \add the Romans\add* gave them letters unto \add the governors of\add* every place, that they should bring them into the land of Judea peaceably.
And this \add is\add* the copy of the letters hich Jonathan rote to the Lacedemonians:
Jonathan the high priest, and the elders of the nation, and the priests, and the other people of the Jes, unto the Lacedemonians \add their\add* brethren \add send\add* greeting:

There ere letters sent in times past unto Onias the high priest from Darius, ho reigned \add then\add* among you, \add to signify\add* that you are our brethren, as the copy \add here\add* underritten doth specify.
At hich time Onias entreated the ambassador that as sent honourably, and received the letters, herein declaration as made of the league and friendship.
Therefore e also, albeit e need none of these \add things\add*, for that e have the holy books \add of scripture\add* in our hands to comfort \add us\add*,

have \add nevertheless\add* attempted to send unto you for the reneing of brotherhood and friendship, lest \add e\add* should become strangers unto you altogether: for there is a long time passed since you sent unto us.

We therefore at all times ithout ceasing, both in \add our\add* feasts, and other convenient days, do remember you in the sacrifices hich e offer, and in \add our\add* prayers, as reason is, and \add as\add* it becometh \add us\add* to think upon \add our\add* brethren:
and e are right glad of your honour.
As for ourselves, e have had great troubles and ars on every side, forsomuch as the kings that are round about us have fought against us.
Hobeit e ould not be troublesome unto you, nor to others of our confederates and friends, in these ars:
for e have help from heaven that succoureth us, so as e are delivered from our enemies, and our enemies are brought under foot.

For this cause e chose Numenius \add the son\add* of Antiochus, and Antipater \add the son\add* of Jason, and sent \add them\add* unto the Romans, to rene the amity that \add e\add* had ith them, and the former league.
We commanded them also to go unto you, and to salute you and to deliver you our letters concerning the reneing of our brotherhood.
Wherefore no ye shall do ell to give us an anser thereto.
And this \add is\add* the copy of the letters hich Oniares sent.
Areus king of the Lacedemonians to Onias the high priest, greeting:
It is found in riting, that the Lacedemonians and Jes are brethren, and that they are of the stock of Abraham:

Then ansered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but hat he seeth the Father do: for hat \add things\add* soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likeise.

that all \add men\add* should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father hich hath sent him.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my ord, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and no is, hen the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.
For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself;
and hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of man.
Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the hich all that are in the graves shall hear his voice,
and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.
I can of mine on self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine on ill, but the ill of the Father hich hath sent me.
If I bear itness of myself, my itness is not true.
There is another that beareth itness of me; and I kno that the itness hich he itnesseth of me is true.
Ye sent unto John, and he bare itness unto the truth.
But I receive not testimony from man: but these \add things\add* I say, that ye might be saved.
He as a burning and a shining light: and ye ere illing for a season to rejoice in his light.
But I have greater itness than \add that of\add* John: for the orks hich the Father hath given me to finish, the same orks that I do, bear itness of me, that the Father hath sent me.
And the Father himself, hich hath sent me, hath borne itness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.
And ye have not his ord abiding in you: for hom he hath sent, him ye believe not.
Search the Scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they hich testify of me.
And ye ill not come to me, that ye might have life.
I receive not honour from men.
But I kno you, that ye have not the love of God in you.
I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his on name, him ye ill receive.
Ho can ye believe, hich receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that \add cometh\add* from God only?
Do not think that I ill accuse you to the Father: there is \add one\add* that accuseth you, \add even\add* Moses, in hom ye trust.
For had ye believed Moses, ye ould have believed me: for he rote of me.
But if ye believe not his ritings, ho shall ye believe my ords?
After these \add things\add* Jesus ent over the sea of Galilee, \add hich is\add* the \add sea\add* of Tiberias.
And a great multitude folloed him, because they sa his miracles hich he did on them that ere diseased.
And Jesus ent up into a mountain, and there he sat ith his disciples.
And the passover, a feast of the Jes, as nigh.
When Jesus then lift up \add his\add* eyes, and sa a great company come unto him, he saith unto Philip, Whence shall e buy bread, that these may eat?
And this he said to prove him: for he himself kne hat he ould do.
Philip ansered him, To hundred pennyorth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little.
One of his disciples, Andre, Simon Peter’s brother, saith unto him,
There is a lad here, hich hath five barley loaves, and to small fishes: but hat are they among so many?
And Jesus said, Make the men sit don. No there as much grass in the place. So the men sat don, \add in\add* number about five thousand.
And Jesus took the loaves; and hen he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that ere set don; and likeise of the fishes as much as they ould.
When they ere filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.
Therefore they gathered \add them\add* together, and filled telve baskets ith the fragments of the five barley loaves, hich remained over and above unto them that had eaten.
Then \add those\add* men, hen they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said, This is of a truth \add that\add* prophet that should come into the orld.
When Jesus therefore perceived that they ould come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.
And hen even as \add no\add* come, his disciples ent don unto the sea,
and entered into a ship, and ent over the sea toards Capernaum. And it as no dark, and Jesus as not come to them.
And the sea arose by reason of a great ind that ble.
So hen they had roed about five and tenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus alking on the sea, and draing nigh unto the ship: and they ere afraid.
But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.
Then they illingly received him into the ship: and immediately the ship as at the land hither they ent.

The day folloing, hen the people hich stood on the other side of the sea sa that there as none other boat there, save that one hereinto his disciples ere entered, and that Jesus ent not ith his disciples into the boat, but \add that\add* his disciples ere gone aay alone;
(hobeit there came other boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place here they did eat bread, after that the Lord had given thanks:)
hen the people therefore sa that Jesus as not there, neither his disciples, they also took shipping, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus.
And hen they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, hen camest thou hither?
Jesus ansered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye sa \add the\add* miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and ere filled.
Labour not for the meat hich perisheth, but for \add that\add* meat hich endureth unto everlasting life, hich the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.
Then said they unto him, What shall e do, that e might ork the orks of God?
Jesus ansered and said unto them, This is the ork of God, that ye believe on \add him\add* hom he hath sent.
They said therefore unto him, What sign sheest thou then, that e may see, and believe thee? hat dost thou ork?
Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is ritten, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not \add that\add* bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is he hich cometh don from heaven, and giveth life unto the orld.
Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.
All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I ill in no ise cast out.
For I came don from heaven, not to do mine on ill, but the ill of him that sent me.
And this is the Father’s ill hich hath sent me, that of all hich he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up \add again\add* at the last day.
And this is the ill of him that sent me, that every one hich seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I ill raise him up \add at\add* the last day.
The Jes then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread hich came don from heaven.
And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, hose father and mother e kno? ho \add is it\add* then \add that\add* he saith, I came don from heaven?
Jesus therefore ansered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.
No \add man\add* can come to me, except the Father hich hath sent me dra him: and I ill raise him up \add at\add* the last day.
It is ritten in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every \add man\add* therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.
Not that any \add man\add* hath seen the Father, save he hich is of God, he hath seen the Father.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.
I am \add that\add* bread of life.
Your fathers did eat manna in the ilderness, and are dead.
This is the bread hich cometh don from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.
I am the living bread hich came don from heaven: if any \add man\add* eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I ill give is my flesh, hich I ill give for the life of the orld.
The Jes therefore strove amongst themselves, saying, Ho can this \add man\add* give us \add his\add* flesh to eat?
Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you.
Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I ill raise him up \add at\add* the last day.
For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, delleth in me, and I in him.
As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me.
This is \add that\add* bread hich came don from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eateth \add of\add* this bread shall live for ever.
These \add things\add* said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
Many therefore of his disciples, hen they had heard \add this\add*, said, This is a hard saying; ho can hear it?
When Jesus kne in himself that his disciples murmured at it, he said unto them, Doth this offend you?
\add What\add* and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up here he as before?
It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the ords that I speak unto you, \add they\add* are spirit, and \add they\add* are life.
But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus kne from the beginning ho they ere that believed not, and ho should betray him.
And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no \add man\add* can come unto me, except it ere given unto him of my Father.
From that \add time\add* many of his disciples ent back, and alked no more ith him.
Then said Jesus unto the telve, Will ye also go aay?
Then Simon Peter ansered him, Lord, to hom shall e go? thou hast the ords of eternal life.
And e believe and are sure that thou art \add that\add* Christ, the Son of the living God.
Jesus ansered them, Have not I chosen you telve, and one of you is a devil?
He spake of Judas Iscariot \add the son\add* of Simon: for he \add it as that\add* should betray him, being one of the telve.
After these \add things\add* Jesus alked in Galilee: for he ould not alk in Jery, because the Jes sought to kill him.
No the Jes’ feast of tabernacles as at hand.
His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see the orks that thou doest.
For \add there is\add* no \add man that\add* doeth any \add thing\add* in secret, and he himself seeketh to be knon openly. If thou do these \add things\add*, she thyself to the orld.
For neither did his brethren believe in him.
Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alay ready.
The orld cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the orks thereof are evil.
Go ye up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast; for my time is not yet full come.
When he had said these \add ords\add* unto them, he abode \add still\add* in Galilee.
But hen his brethren ere gone up, then ent he also up unto the feast, not openly, but as it ere in secret.
Then the Jes sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?
And there as much murmuring among the people concerning him: \add for\add* some said, He is a good \add man:\add* others said, Nay; but he deceiveth the people.
Hobeit no \add man\add* spake openly of him for fear of the Jes.
No about the midst of the feast Jesus ent up into the temple, and taught.
And the Jes marvelled, saying, Ho knoeth this \add man\add* letters, having never learned?
Jesus ansered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.
If any \add man\add* ill do his ill, he shall kno of the doctrine, hether it be of God, or \add hether\add* I speak of myself.
He that speaketh of himself seeketh his on glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
Did not Moses give you the la, and \add yet\add* none of you keepeth the la? Why go ye about to kill me?
The people ansered and said, Thou hast a devil: ho goeth about to kill thee?
Jesus ansered and said unto them, I have done one ork, and ye all marvel.
Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision, not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers; and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.
If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the la of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every hit hole on the sabbath day?
Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
Then said some of them of Jerusalem, Is not this he, hom they seek to kill?
But lo, he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him. Do the rulers kno indeed that this is the very Christ?
Hobeit e kno this \add man\add* hence he is: but hen Christ cometh, no \add man\add* knoeth hence he is.
Then cried Jesus in the temple as he taught, saying, Ye both kno me, and ye kno hence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, hom ye kno not.
But I kno him: for I am from him, and he hath sent me.
Then they sought to take him: but no \add man\add* laid hands on him, because his hour as not yet come.

Ye shall seek me, and shall not find \add me:\add* and here I am, \add thither\add* ye cannot come.
Then said the Jes among themselves, Whither ill he go, that e shall not find him? ill he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?
What \add manner of\add* saying is this that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find \add me:\add* and here I am, \add thither\add* ye cannot come?

He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flo rivers of living ater.
(But this spake he of the Spirit, hich they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost as not yet \add given;\add* because that Jesus as not yet glorified.)

And some of them ould have taken him; but no \add man\add* laid hands on him.

The officers ansered, Never man spake like this man.
Then ansered them the Pharisees, Are ye also deceived?
Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
But this people ho knoeth not the la are cursed.
Nicodemus saith unto them, (he that came to \add Jesus\add* by night, being one of them,)
Doth our la judge any man, before it hear him, and kno hat he doeth?
They ansered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.
And every man ent unto his on house.

And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and he sat don, and taught them.

they say unto him, Master, this oman as taken in adultery, in the very act.

This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped don, and ith \add his\add* finger rote on the ground, \add as though he heard them not\add*.
So hen they continued asking him, he lift up \add himself\add*, and said unto them, He that is ithout sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

And they hich heard \add it\add*, being convicted by \add their on\add* conscience, ent out one by one, beginning at the eldest, \add even\add* unto the last: and Jesus as left alone, and the oman standing in the midst.
When Jesus had lift up \add himself\add*, and sa none but the oman, he said unto her, Woman, here are those thine accusers? hath no \add man\add* condemned thee?
She said, No \add man\add*, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the orld: he that folloeth me shall not alk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
The Pharisees therefore said unto him, Thou bearest record of thyself; thy record is not true.
Jesus ansered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, \add yet\add* my record is true: for I kno hence I came, and hither I go; but ye cannot tell hence I come, and hither I go.
Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no \add man\add*.
And yet if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.
It is also ritten in your la, that the testimony of to men is true.
I am \add one\add* that bear itness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth itness of me.
Then said they unto him, Where is thy Father? Jesus ansered, Ye neither kno me, nor my Father: if ye had knon me, ye should have knon my Father also.
These ords spake Jesus in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no \add man\add* laid hands on him; for his hour as not yet come.
Then said Jesus again unto them, I go my ay, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sins: hither I go, ye cannot come.
Then said the Jes, Will he kill himself? because he saith, Whither I go, ye cannot come.
And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this orld; I am not of this orld.

Then said Jesus unto them, When ye have lift up the Son of man, then shall ye kno that I am \add he\add*, and \add that\add* I do nothing of myself; but as my Father hath taught me, I speak these \add things\add*.

Ye are of \add your\add* father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye ill do. He as a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his on: for he is a liar, and the father of it.

Then ansered the Jes, and said unto him, Say e not ell that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a devil?
Jesus ansered, I have not a devil; but I honour my Father, and ye do dishonour me.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.
Then said the Jes unto him, No e kno that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my saying, he shall never taste of death.
Art thou greater than our father Abraham, hich is dead? and the prophets are dead: hom makest thou thyself?
Jesus ansered, If I honour myself, my honour is nothing: it is my Father that honoureth me; of hom ye say, that he is your God:
yet ye have not knon him; but I kno him: and if I should say, I kno him not, I shall be a liar like unto you: but I kno him, and keep his saying.
Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he sa \add it\add*, and as glad.
Then said the Jes unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?

And as \add Jesus\add* passed by, he sa a man \add hich as\add* blind from \add his\add* birth.

As long as I am in the orld, I am the light of the orld.
When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man ith the clay,
and said unto him, Go, ash in the pool of Siloam, (hich is by interpretation, Sent.) He ent his ay therefore, and ashed, and came seeing.

Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day. Others said, Ho can a man \add that is\add* a sinner do such miracles? And there as a division among them.

Be it knon unto you therefore, men \add and\add* brethren, that through this \add man\add* is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins:

and there they preached the gospel.

\add Which\add* hen the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard \add of\add*, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,

and saying, Sirs, hy do ye these \add things?\add* We also are men of like passions ith you, and preach unto you that \add ye\add* should turn from these vanities unto the living God, hich made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all \add things\add* that are therein:

Nevertheless he left not himself ithout itness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts ith food and gladness.

that the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon hom my name is called, saith the Lord, ho doeth all these \add things\add*.

so \add that\add* not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, hom all Asia and the orld orshippeth.
And hen they heard \add these sayings\add*, they ere full of rath, and cried out, saying, Great \add is\add* Diana of the Ephesians.
And the hole city as filled ith confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed ith one accord into the theatre.
And hen Paul ould have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
And certain of the chief of Asia, hich ere his friends, sent unto him, desiring \add him\add* that \add he\add* ould not adventure himself into the theatre.
Some therefore cried one \add thing\add*, and some another: for the assembly as confused; and the more part kne not herefore they ere come together.
And they dre Alexander out of the multitude, the Jes putting him forard. And Alexander beckoned ith the hand, and ould have made \add his\add* defence unto the people.
But hen \add they\add* kne that he as a Je, all ith one voice about the space of to hours cried out, Great \add is\add* Diana of the Ephesians.

And hen the tonclerk had appeased the people, he said, \add Ye\add* men of Ephesus, hat man is there that knoeth not ho that the city of the Ephesians is a orshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the \add image\add* hich fell don from Jupiter?
Seeing then that these \add things\add* cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
For ye have brought \add hither\add* these men, \add hich are\add* neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen hich are ith him, have a matter against any \add man\add*, the la is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
But if ye inquire any \add thing\add* concerning other \add matters\add*, it shall be determined in a laful assembly.
For e are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause hereby e may give an account of this concourse.
And hen he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
And after the uproar as ceased, Paul called unto \add him\add* the disciples, and embraced \add them\add*, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
And hen he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
and \add there\add* abode three months: and hen the Jes laid ait for him, as he as about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
These going before tarried for us at Troas.
And e sailed aay from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; here e abode seven days.
And upon the first \add day\add* of the eek, hen the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morro; and continued \add his\add* speech until midnight.
And there ere many lights in the upper chamber, here they ere gathered together.

And there sat in a indo a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul as long preaching, he sunk don ith sleep, and fell don from the third loft, and as taken up dead.
And Paul ent don, and fell on him, and embracing \add him\add* said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
When he therefore as come up \add again\add*, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long hile, \add even\add* till break of day, so he departed.
And they brought the young man alive, and ere not a little comforted.
And e ent before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
And hen he met ith us at Assos, e took him in, and came to Mitylene.
And e sailed thence, and came the next \add day\add* over against Chios; and the next \add day\add* e arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next \add day\add* e came to Miletus.
For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he ould not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it ere possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
And hen they ere come to him, he said unto them, Ye kno, from the first day that I came into Asia, after hat manner I have been ith you at all seasons,
serving the Lord ith all humility of mind, and \add ith\add* many tears, and temptations, hich befell me by the lying in ait of the Jes:
\add and\add* ho I kept back nothing that as profitable \add unto you\add*, but have sheed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
testifying both to the Jes, and \add also\add* to the Greeks, repentance toard God, and faith toard our Lord Jesus Christ.
And no behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knoing the \add things\add* that shall befall me there:
save that the Holy Ghost itnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

But none of these \add things\add* move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that \add I\add* might finish my course ith joy, and the ministry, hich I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
And no behold, I kno that ye all, among hom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I \add am\add* pure from the blood of all \add men\add*.
For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the hich the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, hich he hath purchased ith his on blood.
For I kno this, that after my departing shall grievous olves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
Also of your on selves shall men arise, speaking perverse \add things\add*, to dra aay disciples after them.
Therefore atch, and remember, that \add by the space of\add* three years I ceased not to arn every one night and day ith tears.
And no, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the ord of his grace, hich is able to build \add you\add* up, and to give you an inheritance among all them hich are sanctified.
I have coveted no \add man’s\add* silver, or gold, or apparel.
Yea, ye yourselves kno, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that ere ith me.
I have sheed you all \add things\add*, ho that so labouring \add ye\add* ought to support the eak, and to remember the ords of the Lord Jesus, ho he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
And hen he had thus spoken, he kneeled don, and prayed ith them all.
And \add they\add* all ept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
sorroing most \add of all\add* for the ords hich he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
And it came to pass, that after e ere gotten from them, and had launched, e came ith a straight course unto Cos, and the \add day\add* folloing unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
and finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, e ent aboard, and set forth.
No hen e had discovered Cyprus, e left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship as to unlade \add her\add* burden.
And finding disciples, e tarried there seven days: ho said to Paul through the Spirit, that \add he\add* should not go up to Jerusalem.

And hen e had accomplished \add those\add* days, e departed and ent \add our ay;\add* and \add they\add* all brought us on our ay, ith ives and children, till \add e ere\add* out of the city: and e kneeled don on the shore, and prayed.
And hen e had taken our leave one of another, e took ship; and they returned home \add again\add*.
And hen e had finished \add our\add* course from Tyre, e came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode ith them one day.
And the next day e that ere of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cesarea: and e entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, hich as \add one\add* of the seven; and abode ith him.
And the same \add man\add* had four daughters, virgins, hich did prophesy.
And as e tarried \add there\add* many days, there came don from Judea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

And hen he as come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his \add on\add* hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jes at Jerusalem bind the man that oeth this girdle, and shall deliver \add him\add* into the hands of the Gentiles.
And hen e heard these \add things\add*, both e, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
Then Paul ansered, What mean ye to eep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
And hen he ould not be persuaded, e ceased, saying, The ill of the Lord be done.
And after those days e took up our carriages, and ent up to Jerusalem.
There ent ith us also \add certain\add* of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought \add ith them\add* one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, ith hom e should lodge.
And hen e ere come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
And the \add day\add* folloing Paul ent in ith us unto James; and all the elders ere present.
And hen he had saluted them, he declared particularly hat \add things\add* God had rought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
And hen they heard \add it\add*, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, ho many thousands of Jes there are hich believe; and they are all zealous of the la:

and they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jes hich are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they \add ought\add* not to circumcise \add their\add* children, neither to alk after the customs.
What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they ill hear that thou art come.
Do therefore this that e say to thee: We have four men hich have a vo on them;

them take, and purify thyself ith them, and be at charges ith them, that they may shave \add their\add* heads: and all may kno that \add those things\add*, hereof they ere informed concerning thee, are nothing; but \add that\add* thou thyself also alkest orderly, and keepest the la.

As touching the Gentiles hich believe, e have ritten and concluded that they observe no such \add thing\add*, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself ith them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
And hen the seven days ere almost ended, the Jes hich ere of Asia, hen they sa him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all \add men\add* every here against the people, and the la, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
(For they had seen before ith him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, hom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
And all the city as moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and dre him out of the temple: and forthith the doors ere shut.
And as \add they\add* ent about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem as in an uproar.
Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran don unto them: and hen they sa the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded \add him\add* to be bound ith to chains; and demanded ho he as, and hat he had done.
And some cried one \add thing\add*, some another, among the multitude: and hen he could not kno the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
And hen he came upon the stairs, so it as, that he as borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
For the multitude of the people folloed \add after\add*, crying, Aay ith him.
And as Paul as to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
Art not thou \add that\add* Egyptian, hich before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the ilderness four thousand men that ere murderers?
But Paul said, I am a man \add hich am\add* a Je of Tarsus, \add a city\add* in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

And hen he had given \add him\add* licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned ith the hand unto the people. And hen there as made a great silence, he spake unto \add them\add* in the Hebre tongue, saying,
Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence \add hich I make\add* no unto you.
(And hen they heard that he spake in the Hebre tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

I am verily a man \add hich am\add* a Je, born in Tarsus, \add a city\add* in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, \add and\add* taught according to the perfect manner of the la of the fathers, and as zealous toards God, as ye all are this day.
And I persecuted this ay unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and omen.

As also the high priest doth bear me itness, and all the estate of the elders: from hom also I received letters unto the brethren, and ent to Damascus, to bring them hich ere there, bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
And it came to pass that, as I made my journey, and as come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, hy persecutest thou me?
And I ansered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, hom thou persecutest.
And they that ere ith me sa indeed the light, and ere afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all \add things\add* hich are appointed for thee to do.
And hen I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that ere ith me, I came into Damascus.
And one Ananias, a devout man according to the la, having a good report of all the Jes hich delt \add there\add*,
came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that \add thou\add* shouldest kno his ill, and see \add that\add* Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
For thou shalt be his itness unto all men of hat thou hast seen and heard.
And no hy tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and ash aay thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
And it came to pass that, hen I as come again to Jerusalem, even hile I prayed in the temple, I as in a trance;
and sa him saying unto me, Make haste, and get \add thee\add* quickly out of Jerusalem: for they ill not receive thy testimony concerning me.
And I said, Lord, they kno that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
and hen the blood of thy martyr Stephen as shed, I also as standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that sle him.
And he said unto me, Depart: for I ill send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
And they gave him audience unto this ord, and \add then\add* lift up their voices, and said, Aay ith such \add a fello\add* from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
And as they cried out, and cast \add off their\add* clothes, and thre dust into the air,
the chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might kno herefore they cried so against him.
And as they bound him ith thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood \add by\add*, Is it laful for you to scourge a man \add that is\add* a Roman, and uncondemned?
When the centurion heard \add that\add*, he ent and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed hat thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
And the chief captain ansered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I as \add free\add* born.
Then straightay they departed from him hich should have examined him: and the chief captain also as afraid, after he kne that he as a Roman, and because he had bound him.

On the morro, because he ould have knon the certainty herefore he as accused of the Jes, he loosed him from \add his\add* bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul don, and set \add him\add* before them.
And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men \add and\add* brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, \add thou\add* hited all: for sittest thou to judge me after the la, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the la?
And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
Then said Paul, I ist not, brethren, that he as the high priest: for it is ritten, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

But hen Paul perceived that the one part ere Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men \add and\add* brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
And hen he had so said, there arose a dissension beteen the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude as divided.
For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

And there arose a great cry: and the scribes \add that ere\add* of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

And hen there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go don, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring \add him\add* into the castle.
And the night folloing the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear itness also at Rome.
And hen it as day, certain of the Jes banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that \add they\add* ould neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
And they ere more \add than\add* forty hich had made this conspiracy.
And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that \add e\add* ill eat nothing until e have slain Paul.

No therefore ye ith the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him don unto you to morro, as though ye ould inquire something more perfectly concerning him: and e, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
And hen Paul’s sister’s son heard of \add their\add* lying in ait, he ent and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
Then Paul called one of the centurions unto \add him\add*, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain \add thing\add* to tell him.

So he took him, and brought \add him\add* to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto \add him\add*, and prayed \add me\add* to bring this young man unto thee, ho hath something to say unto thee.
Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and ent \add ith him\add* aside privately, and asked \add him\add*, What is that thou hast to tell me?
And he said, The Jes have agreed to desire thee that thou ouldest bring don Paul to morro into the council, as though they ould inquire somehat of him more perfectly.

But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in ait for him of them moe \add than\add* forty men, hich have bound themselves ith an oath, that \add they\add* ill neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and no are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged \add him, See thou\add* tell no \add man\add* that thou hast sheed these \add things\add* to me.

And he called unto \add him\add* to centurions, saying, Make ready to hundred soldiers to go to Cesarea, and horsemen threescore \add and\add* ten, and spearmen to hundred, at the third hour of the night;
and provide \add them\add* beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring \add him\add* safe unto Felix the governor.
And he rote a letter after this manner:
Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix \add sendeth\add* greeting.
This man as taken of the Jes, and should have been killed of them: then came I ith an army, and rescued him, having understood that he as a Roman.
And hen I ould have knon the cause herefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
hom I perceived to be accused of questions of their la, but to have nothing laid to his charge orthy of death or of bonds.

And hen it as told me ho that the Jes laid ait for the man, I sent straightay to thee, and gave commandment to \add his\add* accusers also to say before thee hat \add they had\add* against him. Fareell.
Then the soldiers, as it as commanded them, took Paul, and brought \add him\add* by night to Antipatris.
On the morro they left the horsemen to go ith him, and returned to the castle:
ho, hen they came to Cesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
And hen the governor had read \add the letter\add*, he asked of hat province he as: and hen he understood that \add he as\add* of Cilicia;
I ill hear thee, said he, hen thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
And after five days Ananias the high priest descended ith the elders, and \add ith\add* a certain orator \add named\add* Tertullus, ho informed the governor against Paul.

And hen he as called \add forth\add*, Tertullus began to accuse \add him\add*, saying, Seeing that by thee e enjoy great quietness, and that very orthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
e accept \add it\add* alays, and in all places, most noble Felix, ith all thankfulness.
Notithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray \add thee\add* that thou ouldest hear us of thy clemency a fe ords.
For e have found this man a pestilent \add fello\add*, and a mover of sedition among all the Jes throughout the orld, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
ho also hath gone about to profane the temple: hom e took, and ould have judged according to our la.
But the chief captain Lysias came \add upon us\add*, and ith great violence took \add him\add* aay out of our hands,
commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of hom thyself mayest take knoledge of all these \add things\add*, hereof e accuse him.
And the Jes also assented, saying that these \add things\add* ere so.
Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, ansered, Forasmuch as I kno that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully anser for myself:
because that thou mayest understand, that there are \add yet\add* but telve days since I ent up to Jerusalem for to orship.
And they neither found me in the temple disputing ith any \add man\add*, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
neither can they prove \add the things\add* hereof they no accuse me.
But this I confess unto thee, that after the ay hich they call heresy, so orship I the God of my fathers, believing all \add things\add* hich are ritten in the la and the prophets:
and have hope toards God, hich they themselves also allo, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
And herein do I exercise myself, to have alays a conscience void of offence toard God, and \add toard\add* men.
No after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
Whereupon certain Jes from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither ith multitude, nor ith tumult.
Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
Or else let these same \add here\add* say, if they have found any evil doing in me, hile I stood before the council,
except \add it be\add* for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

And hen Felix heard these \add things\add*, having more perfect knoledge of \add that\add* ay, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come don, I ill kno the uttermost of your matter.
And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let \add him\add* have liberty, and that \add he\add* should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
And after certain days, hen Felix came ith his ife Drusilla, hich as a Jeess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and ansered, Go \add thy ay\add* for \add this\add* time; hen I have a convenient season, I ill call for thee.
He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: herefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed ith him.
But after to years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, illing to she the Jes a pleasure, left Paul bound.
No hen Festus as come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cesarea to Jerusalem.
Then the high priest and the chief of the Jes informed him against Paul, and besought him,
and desired favour against him, that he ould send for him to Jerusalem, laying ait in the ay to kill him.
But Festus ansered, that Paul should be kept at Cesarea, and that he himself ould depart shortly \add thither\add*.
Let them therefore, said he, hich among you are able, go don ith \add me\add*, and accuse this man, if there be any \add ickedness\add* in him.
And hen he had tarried among them more than ten days, he ent don unto Cesarea; and the next day sitting in the judgment seat, commanded Paul to be brought.
And hen he as come, the Jes hich came don from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, hich they could not prove.
While he ansered for himself, Neither against the la of the Jes, neither against the temple, nor \add yet\add* against Cesar, have I offended any \add thing at all\add*.
But Festus, illing to do the Jes a pleasure, ansered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these \add things\add* before me?
Then said Paul, I stand at Cesar’s judgment seat, here I ought to be judged: to the Jes have I done no rong, as thou very ell knoest.

For if I be an offender, or have committed any \add thing\add* orthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none \add of these things\add* hereof these accuse me, no \add man\add* may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cesar.
Then Festus, hen he had conferred ith the council, ansered, Hast thou appealed unto Cesar? unto Cesar shalt thou go.
And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cesarea to salute Festus.
And hen they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
about hom, hen I as at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jes informed \add me\add*, desiring \add to have\add* judgment against him.

To hom I ansered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he hich is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to anser for himself concerning the crime laid \add against him\add*.
Therefore, hen they ere come hither, ithout any delay, on the morro I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought \add forth\add*.
Against hom hen the accusers stood \add up\add*, they brought none accusation of \add such things\add* as I supposed:
but had certain questions against him of their on superstition, and of one Jesus, \add hich as\add* dead, hom Paul affirmed to be alive.
And because I doubted of such \add manner of\add* questions, I asked \add him\add* hether he ould go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these \add matters\add*.
But hen Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cesar.
Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I ould also hear the man myself. To morro, said he, thou shalt hear him.

And on the morro, hen Agrippa as come, and Bernice, ith great pomp, and ere entered into the place of hearing, ith the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul as brought \add forth\add*.

And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men hich are here present ith us, ye see this \add man\add*, about hom all the multitude of the Jes have dealt ith me, both at Jerusalem, and \add also\add* here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

Of hom I have no certain \add thing\add* to rite unto \add my\add* lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somehat to rite.

I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall anser for myself this day before thee touching all \add the things\add* hereof I am accused of the Jes:

My manner of life from \add my\add* youth, hich as at the first among mine on nation at Jerusalem, kno all the Jes;
