For the king knoeth of these \add things\add*, before hom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these \add things\add* are hidden from him; for this \add thing\add* as not done in a corner.

and hen they ere gone aside, they talked beteen themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing orthy of death or of bonds.

and, hardly passing it, came unto a place \add hich is\add* called The fair havens; nigh hereunto as the city \add of\add* Lasea.

And Paul delt to hole years in his on hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

\sc Paul\sc*, a servant of Jesus Christ, called \add to be\add* an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
(hich he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, hich as made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
\add and\add* declared \add to be\add* the Son of God ith poer, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
by hom e have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
among hom are ye also \add the\add* called of Jesus Christ:
to all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called \add to be\add* saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the hole orld.
For God is my itness, hom I serve ith my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that ithout ceasing I make mention of you, alays in my prayers,
making request, if by any means no at length I might have a prosperous journey by the ill of God to come unto you.
For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end you may be established;
that is, that \add I\add* may be comforted together ith you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
No I ould not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but as let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.
I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the barbarians; both to the ise, and to the unise.
So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the poer of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Je first, and \add also\add* to the Greek.
For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is ritten, The just shall live by faith.
For the rath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, ho hold the truth in unrighteousness;

For the invisible \add things\add* of him from the creation of the orld are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, \add even\add* his eternal poer and Godhead; so that they are ithout excuse:
because that, hen they kne God, they glorified \add him\add* not as God, neither ere thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart as darkened.
Professing \add themselves\add* to be ise, they became fools,
and changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their on hearts, to dishonour their on bodies beteen themselves:
ho changed the truth of God into a lie, and orshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, ho is blessed for ever. Amen.
For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their omen did change the natural use into that hich is against nature:

and likeise also the men, leaving the natural use of the oman, burned in their lust one toards another; men ith men orking that hich is unseemly, and receiving in themselves \add that\add* recompence of their error hich as meet.
And even as they did not like to retain God in \add their\add* knoledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those \add things\add* hich are not convenient;
being filled ith all unrighteousness, fornication, ickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; hisperers,
backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil \add things\add*, disobedient to parents,
ithout understanding, covenant-breakers, ithout natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
ho knoing the judgment of God, that they hich commit such \add things\add* are orthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do \add them\add*.
Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, hosoever thou art that judgest: for herein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same \add things\add*.
But e are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them hich commit such \add things\add*.
And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them hich do such \add things\add*, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knoing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself rath against the day of rath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
ho ill render to every \add man\add* according to his deeds:
to them ho by patient continuance in ell doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
but unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and rath,
tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Je first, and \add also\add* of the Gentile;
but glory, honour, and peace, to every \add man\add* that orketh good, to the Je first, and \add also\add* to the Gentile:
for there is no respect of persons ith God.
For as many as have sinned ithout la shall also perish ithout la: and as many as have sinned in the la shall be judged by the la;
(for not the hearers of the la \add are\add* just before God, but the doers of the la shall be justified.
For hen \add the\add* Gentiles, hich have not the la, do by nature the \add things\add* contained in the la, these, having not the la, are a la unto themselves:
hich she the ork of the la ritten in their hearts, their conscience also bearing itness, and \add their\add* thoughts the mean hile accusing or else excusing one another;)
in the day hen God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.
Behold, thou art called a Je, and restest in the la, and makest thy boast of God,
and knoest \add his\add* ill, and approvest the \add things\add* that are more excellent, being instructed out of the la;
and art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them hich are in darkness,
an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, hich hast the form of knoledge and of the truth in the la.
Thou therefore hich teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest \add a man\add* should not steal, dost thou steal?
Thou that sayest \add a man\add* should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the la: but if thou be a breaker of the la, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.

but he \add is\add* a Je, hich is one inardly; and circumcision \add is that\add* of the heart, in the spirit, \add and\add* not \add in\add* the letter; hose praise \add is\add* not of men, but of God.

Much every ay: chiefly, because that unto them ere committed the oracles of God.

But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, hat shall e say? \add Is\add* God unrighteous ho taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man)

For if the truth of God hath \add more\add* abounded through my lie unto his glory; hy yet am I also judged as a sinner?
And not \add rather\add*, (as e be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that e say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? hose damnation is just.
What then? are e better \add than they?\add* No, in no ise: for e have before proved both Jes and Gentiles, that \add they\add* are all under sin;
as it is ritten, There is none righteous, no, not one:
there is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.
They are all gone out of the ay, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
Their throat \add is\add* an open sepulchre; ith their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps \add is\add* under their lips:
hose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
their feet \add are\add* sift to shed blood:
destruction and misery \add are\add* in their ays:
and the ay of peace have they not knon:
there is no fear of God before their eyes.
No e kno that hat \add things\add* soever the la saith, it saith to them ho are under the la: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the orld may become guilty before God.
Therefore by the deeds of the la there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the la \add is\add* the knoledge of sin.
But no the righteousness of God ithout the la is manifested, being itnessed by the la and the prophets;
even the righteousness of God \add hich is\add* by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:
for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:
hom God hath set forth \add to be\add* a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;
to declare, \add I say\add*, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him hich believeth in Jesus.

\add Is he\add* the God of the Jes only? \add is he\add* not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:
seeing \add it is\add* one God, hich shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
Do e then make void the la through faith? God forbid: yea, e establish the la.
What shall e say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
For if Abraham ere justified by orks, he hath hereof to glory; but not before God.
For hat saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it as counted unto him for righteousness.
No to him that orketh is the reard not reckoned of grace, but of debt.
But to him that orketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto hom God imputeth righteousness ithout orks,
\add saying\add*, Blessed \add are they\add* hose iniquities are forgiven, and hose sins are covered.
Blessed \add is\add* the man to hom the Lord ill not impute sin.
\add Cometh\add* this blessedness then upon the circumcision \add only\add*, or upon the uncircumcision also? for e say that faith as reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith hich he had \add yet\add* being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:
and the father of circumcision to them ho are not of the circumcision only, but ho also alk in the steps of \add that\add* faith of our father Abraham, hich he had being \add yet\add* uncircumcised.
For the promise, that he should be the heir of the orld, \add as\add* not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the la, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if they hich are of the la \add be\add* heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:
because the la orketh rath: for here no la is, \add there is\add* no transgression.

Therefore \add it is\add* of faith, that \add it might be\add* by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only hich is of the la, but to that also hich is of the faith of Abraham; ho is the father of us all,

(as it is ritten, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before \add him\add* hom he believed, \add even\add* God, ho quickeneth the dead, and calleth those \add things\add* hich be not as though they ere.
Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations; according to that hich as spoken, So shall thy seed be.
And being not eak in faith, he considered not his on body no dead, hen he as about an hundred year old, neither \add yet\add* the deadness of Sara’s omb:

and being fully persuaded that, hat he had promised, he as able also to perform.

No as touching things offered unto idols, e kno that e all have knoledge. Knoledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

To the eak became I as eak, that I might gain the eak: I am made all \add things\add* to all \add men\add*, that I might by all means save some.
And this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I might be partaker thereof ith \add you\add*.
Kno ye not that they hich run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.

\add And\add* even \add things\add* ithout life giving sound, hether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, ho shall it be knon hat is piped or harped?

Therefore if I kno not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh \add shall be\add* a barbarian unto me.

What is it then? I ill pray ith the spirit, and ill pray ith the understanding also: I ill sing ith the spirit, and I ill sing ith the understanding also.
Else hen thou shalt bless ith the spirit, ho shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not hat thou sayest?
For thou verily givest thanks ell, but the other is not edified.
I thank my God, I speak ith tongues more than you all:

Brethren, be not children in understanding: hobeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.
In the la it is ritten, With \add men\add* of other tongues and other lips ill I speak unto this people; and yet for all that ill they not hear me, saith the Lord.

If therefore the hole church be come together into one place, and all speak ith tongues, and there come in \add those that are\add* unlearned, or unbelievers, ill they not say that ye are mad?
But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or \add one\add* unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:
and thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling don on \add his\add* face he ill orship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

Ho is it then, brethren? hen ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all \add things\add* be done unto edifying.
If any \add man\add* speak in an \add unknon\add* tongue, \add let it be\add* by to, or at the most \add by\add* three, and \add that\add* by course; and let one interpret.

For ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.
And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets:
for God is not \add the author\add* of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
Let your omen keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but \add they are commanded\add* to be under obedience, as also saith the la.
And if they ill learn any \add thing\add*, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for omen to speak in the church.
What? came the ord of God out from you? or came it unto you only?

But if any \add man\add* be ignorant, let him be ignorant.

Let all \add things\add* be done decently and in order.
Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel hich I preached unto you, hich also you have received, and herein ye stand;
by hich also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory hat I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.
For I delivered unto you first \add of all\add* that hich I also received, ho that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
and that he as buried, and that he rose \add again\add* the third day according to the scriptures:
and that he as seen of Cephas, then of the telve:
after that, he as seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of hom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.

And last of all he as seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.
For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by the grace of God I am hat I am: and his grace hich as \add bestoed\add* upon me as not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God hich as ith me.
Therefore hether \add it ere\add* I or they, so e preach, and so ye believed.
No if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, ho say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?

and if Christ be not risen, then \add is\add* our preaching vain, and your faith \add is\add* also vain.

ho gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good orks.
These \add things\add* speak, and exhort, and rebuke ith all authority. Let no \add man\add* despise thee.
Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and poers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good ork,

not by orks of righteousness hich e have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the ashing of regeneration, and reneing of the Holy Ghost;
hich he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;

\add This is\add* a faithful saying, and these \add things\add* I ill that thou affirm constantly, that they hich have believed in God might be careful to maintain good orks. These \add things\add* are good and profitable unto men.

A man \add that is\add* a heretick, after the first and second admonition, reject;
knoing that \add he that is\add* such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.
When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to inter.
Bring Zenas the layer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be anting unto them.
And let ours also learn to maintain good orks for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.

All that are ith me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace \add be\add* ith you all. Amen. \b \mi ¶ It as ritten to Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretians, from Nicopolis of Macedonia.
\sc Paul\sc*, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy \add our\add* brother, unto Philemon \add our\add* dearly beloved, and fellolabourer,
and to \add our\add* beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellosoldier, and to the church in thy house:
Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God, making mention of thee alays in my prayers,
hearing of thy love and faith, hich thou hast toard the Lord Jesus, and toard all saints;

Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that hich is convenient,
\add yet\add* for love’s sake I rather beseech \add thee\add*, being such a one as Paul the aged, and no also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, hom I have begotten in my bonds:

If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
If he hath ronged thee, or oeth \add thee\add* ought, put that on mine account;
I Paul have ritten \add it\add* ith mine on hand, I ill repay \add it:\add* albeit I do not say to thee ho thou oest unto me even thine on self besides.
Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my boels in the Lord.
Having confidence in thy obedience I rote unto thee, knoing that thou ilt also do more than I say.
But ithal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
There salute thee Epaphras, my felloprisoner in Christ Jesus;
Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellolabourers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ \add be\add* ith your spirit. Amen. \b \mi ¶ Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.
\sc God\sc*, ho at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,

ho being the brightness of \add his\add* glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all \add things\add* by the ord of his poer, hen he had by himself purged our sins, sat don on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
For unto hich of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I ill be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?
And again, hen he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the orld, he saith, And let all the angels of God orship him.
And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
But unto the Son \add he saith\add*, Thy throne, O God, \add is\add* for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness \add is\add* the sceptre of thy kingdom.
Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, \add even\add* thy God, hath anointed thee \add ith\add* the oil of gladness above thy fellos.
And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the orks of thine hands:
they shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall ax old as \add doth\add* a garment;
and as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
But to hich of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?
Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them ho shall be heirs of salvation?
Therefore e ought to give the more earnest heed to the \add things\add* hich e have heard, lest at any time e should let \add them\add* slip.
For if the ord spoken by angels as stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reard;
ho shall e escape, if e neglect so great salvation; hich at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and as confirmed unto us by them that heard \add him;\add*
God also bearing \add them\add* itness, both ith signs and onders, and ith divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his on ill?
For unto \add the\add* angels hath he not put in subjection the orld to come, hereof e speak:
but one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
Thou madest him a little loer than the angels; thou cronedst him ith glory and honour, and didst set him over the orks of thy hands:

thou hast put all \add things\add* in subjection under his feet. For in that \add he\add* put all in subjection under him, he left nothing \add that is\add* not put under him. But no e see not yet all \add things\add* put under him.

For it became him, for hom \add are\add* all \add things\add*, and by hom \add are\add* all \add things\add*, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

And again, I ill put my trust in him. And again, Behold, I, and the children hich God hath given me.
Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likeise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the poer of death, that is, the devil;
and deliver them ho through fear of death ere all their lifetime subject to bondage.

Wherefore in all \add things\add* it behoved him to be made like unto \add his\add* brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest \add in things\add* pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
ho as faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses \add as faithful\add* in all his house.
For this \add man\add* as counted orthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he ho hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.
For every house is builded by some \add man;\add* but he that built all \add things is\add* God.
And Moses verily \add as\add* faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those \add things\add* hich ere to be spoken after;
but Christ as a Son over his on house; hose house are e, if e hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.
Wherefore, as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye ill hear his voice,
harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the ilderness:
hen your fathers tempted me, proved me, and sa my orks forty years.
Wherefore I as grieved ith that generation, and said, They do alay err in \add their\add* heart; and they have not knon my ays.
So I sare in my rath, They shall not enter into my rest.

But exhort one another daily, hile it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
For e are made partakers of Christ, if e hold the beginning of \add our\add* confidence stedfast unto the end;
hilst it is said, To day if ye ill hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
For some, hen they had heard, did provoke: hobeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
But ith hom as he grieved forty years? \add as it\add* not ith them that had sinned, hose carcases fell in the ilderness?
And to hom sare he that \add they\add* should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
So e see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left \add us\add* of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short \add of it\add*.
For unto us as the gospel preached, as ell as unto them: but the ord preached did not profit them, not being mixed ith faith in them that heard \add it\add*.
For e hich have believed do enter into rest, as \add he\add* said, As I have sorn in my rath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the orks ere finished from the foundation of the orld.
For \add he\add* spake in a certain place of the seventh \add day\add* on this ise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his orks.
And in this \add place\add* again, If they shall enter into my rest.
Seeing therefore it remaineth that some \add must\add* enter therein, and they to hom it as first preached entered not in because of unbelief,

For if Jesus had given them rest, \add then\add* ould he not afterard have spoken of another day.
There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his on orks, as God \add did\add* from his.
Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any \add man\add* fall after the same example of unbelief.

For the ord of God \add is\add* quick, and poerful, and sharper than any toedged sord, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marro, and \add is\add* a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
Neither is there any creature \add that is\add* not manifest in his sight: but all \add things are\add* naked and opened unto the eyes of him ith hom e have to do.
Seeing then that e have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast \add our\add* profession.
For e have not a high priest hich cannot be touched ith the feeling of our infirmities; but as in all \add points\add* tempted like as \add e are, yet\add* ithout sin.

For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men \add in things\add* pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
ho can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the ay; for that he himself also is compassed ith infirmity.
And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
And no \add man\add* taketh \add this\add* honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as \add as\add* Aaron.
So also Christ glorified not himself to be made a high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
As he saith also in another \add place\add*, Thou \add art\add* a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
Who in the days of his flesh, hen he had offered up prayers and supplications ith strong crying and tears unto him that as able to save him from death, and as heard in that \add he\add* feared;
though he ere a Son, \add yet\add* learned he obedience by \add the things\add* hich he suffered;
and being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;

Of hom e have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

For hen for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that \add one\add* teach you again hich \add be\add* the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.

of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

For the earth hich drinketh \add in\add* the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by hom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
but that hich beareth thorns and briers \add is\add* rejected, and \add is\add* nigh unto cursing; hose end \add is\add* to be burned.

that ye be not slothful, but folloers of them ho through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For hen God made promise to Abraham, because he could sear by no greater, he sare by himself,

hich \add hope\add* e have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and hich entereth into that ithin the vail;

For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, ho met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
to hom also Abraham gave a tenth \add part\add* of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, hich is, King of peace;
ithout father, ithout mother, ithout descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.

And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, ho receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the la, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:

If therefore perfection ere by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the la,) hat further need \add as there\add* that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

(for those priests ere made ithout an oath; but this ith an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sare and ill not repent, Thou \add art\add* a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)

For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: herefore \add it is\add* of necessity that this \add man\add* have somehat also to offer.

ho serve unto the example and shado of heavenly \add things\add*, as Moses as admonished of God hen he as about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith \add he, that\add* thou make all \add things\add* according to the pattern sheed to thee in the mount.

For this \add is\add* the covenant that I ill make ith the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I ill put my las into their mind, and rite them in their hearts: and I ill be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:

For I ill be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities ill I remember no more.
In that \add he\add* saith, A ne \add covenant\add*, he hath made the first old. No that hich decayeth and axeth old \add is\add* ready to vanish aay.

hich had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about ith gold, herein \add as\add* the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;

No hen these \add things\add* ere thus ordained, the priests ent alays into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service \add of God\add*.
But into the second \add ent\add* the high priest alone once every year, not ithout blood, hich he offered for himself, and \add for\add* the errors of the people:
the Holy Ghost this signifying, that the ay into the holiest \add of all\add* as not yet made manifest, hile as the first tabernacle as yet standing:
hich \add as\add* a figure for the time \add then\add* present, in hich ere offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
\add hich stood\add* only in meats and drinks, and divers ashings, and carnal ordinances, imposed \add on them\add* until the time of reformation.
But Christ being come a high priest of good \add things\add* to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made ith hands, that is to say, not of this building,
neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his on blood he entered in once into the holy \add place\add*, having obtained eternal redemption \add for us\add*.

And for this cause he is the mediator of the ne testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that ere under the first testament, they hich are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

For hen Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the la, he took the blood of calves and of goats, ith ater, and scarlet ool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
saying, This \add is\add* the blood of the testament hich God hath enjoined unto you.

And almost all \add things\add* are by the la purged ith blood; and ithout shedding of blood is no remission.
\add It as\add* therefore necessary that the patterns of \add things\add* in the heavens should be purified ith these; but the heavenly \add things\add* themselves ith better sacrifices than these.
For Christ is not entered into the holy \add places\add* made ith hands, \add hich are\add* the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, no to appear in the presence of God for us:
nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy \add place\add* every year ith blood of others;
for then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the orld: but no once in the end of the orld hath he appeared to put aay sin by the sacrifice of himself.
And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
so Christ as once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time ithout sin unto salvation.

For the la having a shado of good \add things\add* to come, \add and\add* not the very image of the things, can never ith those sacrifices hich they offered year by year continually make the comers \add thereunto\add* perfect.
For then ould they not have ceased to be offered? because that the orshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
But in those \add sacrifices there is\add* a remembrance \add again made\add* of sins every year.
For \add it is\add* not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take aay sins.
Wherefore hen he cometh into the orld, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou ouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
in burnt offerings and \add sacrifices\add* for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is ritten of me,) to do thy ill, O God.
Above hen he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and \add offering\add* for sin thou ouldest not, neither hadst pleasure \add therein:\add* hich are offered by the la;
then said he, Lo, I come to do thy ill, O God. He taketh aay the first, that he may establish the second.
By the hich ill e are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

but this \add man\add*, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat don on the right hand of God;
from henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
\add Whereof\add* the Holy Ghost also is a itness to us: for after that \add he\add* had said before,
This \add is\add* the covenant that I ill make ith them after those days, saith the Lord, I ill put my las into their hearts, and in their minds ill I rite them;
and their sins and iniquities ill I remember no more.
No here remission of these \add is, there is\add* no more offering for sin.
Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
\add by\add* a ne and living ay, hich he hath consecrated for us, through the vail, that is to say, his flesh;
and \add having\add* a high priest over the house of God;

of ho much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought orthy, ho hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, hereith he as sanctified, an unholy \add thing\add*, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?

For ye had compassion \add of me\add* in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knoing in yourselves that \add ye\add* have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.

For ye kno ho that afterard, hen he ould have inherited the blessing, he as rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully ith tears.

Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.

\sc James\sc*, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the telve tribes hich are scattered abroad, greeting.

From hence \add come\add* ars and fightings among you? \add come they\add* not hence, \add even\add* of your lusts that ar in your members?

And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

let him kno, that he hich converteth the sinner from the error of his ay shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.

that the trial of your faith, \add being\add* much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried ith fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:
